Perhaps a problem that has long seemed stuck will begin to show a way forward once we are willing to pause and listen.
CORE WISDOM

Ibn 'Ata'illah describes a knower never losing need for Allah or relying absolutely on anything besides Him. Need remains in ease. We learn awareness so success does not make the heart claim independence. Means are used well and people appreciated, while acknowledgement of Allah's sustaining care accompanies daily decisions.

Someone knowing Allah does more than ask when every path feels closed. In success and abundant resources, they still recognize fundamental need. This wisdom describes that maturity, so smooth circumstances do not make the heart feel sufficient through personal ability or created help.

Idtirar means profound need and inability to stand independently. Qarar means settling or finding comfort in a support. The heart of an 'arif, one knowing Allah, never loses awareness of needing Him. Its highest peace does not depend on anything besides Allah, although it still uses means and appreciates helpers.

Let us slow down for a moment, dear congregation. The terms in these sayings help us recognize the movements of the heart, but we need not feel intimidated by the terminology. Notice its connection with maintaining awareness of need for Allah in smooth times. Once we understand the meaning, examine the actions we can see: what words are spoken, what decisions are made, and who experiences the consequences. That is where understanding begins to take shape. If it is not yet clear, go through the explanation again. Learning our religion requires patience. We can also ask respectfully when a sentence seems confusing, so that eagerness to practise is accompanied by sound understanding.
EXAMPLES AND CONVERSATION WITH THE CONGREGATION

Dear friends, in good circumstances keep learning about your trusts. Do not reject input because of past success. Change can occur and abilities need renewal. We can also help others within ability without feeling their saviour. Help respectfully, because we ourselves still receive much assistance not entirely visible or individually nameable.

“If I always feel need, will I lose confidence?” We can still use abilities firmly. Acknowledging limits makes decisions more honest. We know what we understand and what needs asking. Healthy confidence does not require denying Allah's help or others' work. Ability can be appreciated and developed while remaining open to improvement.

Work progresses and several decisions produce good results. We begin feeling everything understood, quickly dismissing input. Dear friends, gratitude for smooth circumstances includes openness to learning. Skills need renewal and circumstances can change. Hear correction without sheltering behind old success. We can help others without claiming to be their sole support. Many resources easing today were themselves help previously received. Remembering makes confidence more honest, seeing ability alongside limits and accompanying help.

“If I always feel need, will I hesitate to act?” Acknowledging limits does not require every step to be doubtful, dear congregation. We can act firmly where informed and seek explanation elsewhere. This wisdom affirms need for Allah even in spacious circumstances. No major disruption is needed before remembering Him. This belief directs effort without arrogance. Nor should apparent calm be labelled forgetfulness of Allah. Examination concerns ourselves: am I still willing to pray, learn, and acknowledge help making work possible?

Dear congregation, some questions look simple, but we only feel their weight when living through them: “What needs maintaining when plans succeed and needs are met?” Let us give ourselves time to consider this. We may picture ourselves or someone who needs support. We are learning to answer in words that can be put into practice. Avoid an answer that makes every problem seem resolved in a single breath. Some matters need time and support. Even so, that process can begin with a small decision. Try finding that decision in the earlier example. This is where our conversation becomes useful for life after the gathering ends.
PERSONAL REFLECTION

Someone earning well still maintains supplication, honesty, and willingness to learn. They know working ability can change and much lies beyond control. That awareness makes success easier to appreciate without arrogance. When human help arrives, they give thanks while recognizing it as a provided means.

Dear congregation, smooth family circumstances offer good time to build habits. Pray together as appropriate, discuss trusts, and practise fair task sharing. Do not wait for crisis to begin listening. Relationships cared for in calm can help face difficulty more orderly. We prepare beyond knowing when problems come: today's trust already deserves care.

Dear congregation, try looking at our own journey with both honesty and compassion. In the matter of maintaining awareness of need for Allah in smooth times, we may have made small progress for which we have never given thanks. There may also be a mistake we keep wanting to hide. Both can teach us without being put on display. Give thanks for the help that has already come, then examine what needs improving. Do not compare our whole journey with a fragment of someone else's life. We have real responsibilities today. Recognizing our part allows reflection to move into action, so regret need not remain a thought circling endlessly without direction.

Dear friends, we can pause before answering a question that feels close to home. Sometimes our first answer comes from a habit of defending ourselves. Given time, we can hear the advice more clearly. We do not have to make everyone speak immediately. Some people think more easily in silence, while others are helped by asking questions. What matters is making room to understand, then choosing a step sincerely. We want to learn in a way that preserves good manners and makes our responsibilities clearer.
PRACTICAL STEPS TO TRY

Practise remembering Allah on ordinary days too. Seek protection before problems and use ease to fulfil unfinished rights. If one support is lost, allow sadness and seek a good path. Need for Allah does not conflict with courage to act. It directs action away from making means absolute. This wisdom builds deeper steadfastness because relationship with Allah lives through ease and constraint, rather than only when no other choice seems available.

For practice, choose one supplication and evaluation habit to preserve in good times. Appreciate helpers and listen earnestly to one suggestion. When assisting, respect recipients' agency over their lives. Success may inform learning without becoming an absolute guarantee. May ease increase gratitude and humility, and may awareness of needing Allah accompany confident, orderly actions respecting surrounding people's rights.

Dear friends, test our plan against everyday situations. When we face the matter of maintaining awareness of need for Allah in smooth times again, what will change in our actions? Choose an answer we can recognize, such as having a conversation or stopping a habit. If the answer is still too general, make the step smaller. We are not writing a beautiful promise for others. We are preparing help for ourselves when we encounter an old habit. After doing it, give thanks and keep learning. If it has not worked yet, examine the reason honestly, then try again with preparation better suited to the situation.

Let us leave room for questions that remain unresolved, dear congregation. If confusion remains after the gathering, write down the issue clearly. Then ask someone who understands the subject and knows the circumstances involved. We may learn gradually. A little accurate understanding is more helpful than a rushed decision made simply because we want to feel that everything is settled. Meanwhile, continue fulfilling our clear obligations and respect the rights of those around us.
REINFORCING THE MESSAGE AND CLOSING SUPPLICATION

Let us recall the direction of today's discussion, dear congregation. The lesson about maintaining awareness of need for Allah in smooth times invites us to examine our own choices and improve what is our responsibility. After returning home, things may feel ordinary again. That is where a good intention needs attention. We can remind ourselves gently while remaining firm about our obligations. If we need to begin again one day, let us begin. The opportunity to learn is not exhausted because one attempt has not gone smoothly. While we have the ability and opportunity, let us keep seeking goodness and asking Allah to guide our hearts and accept our deeds.

Let us humble our hearts when life is easy. May Allah preserve beneficial ease, protect against self-sufficiency, and guide blessings' use. May success increase willingness to learn and sensitivity to help. May need for Him remain recognized in calm, so supplication appears before every relied-upon method reveals its limits. Amin.
Wassalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh.
phrasesEn: الْعَارِفُ لَا يَزُولُ اضْطِرَارُهُ،
The knower of Allah never loses profound need for Him.
وَلَا يَكُونُ مَعَ غَيْرِ اللَّهِ قَرَارُهُ.
Their heart does not settle in comfort through dependence on anything besides Allah.

114.translation: He illuminates outward reality with the light of the traces of His creation, and illuminates inner secrets with the light of His attributes. Outward light can therefore set, while the light of hearts and inner secrets does not set. Thus it is said: the daytime sun sets at night, but the sun of hearts never sets.
syarahEn: Sunlight helps eyes see objects, but clarity about life's direction needs another illumination. Someone can stand in a bright place yet remain confused about what is right. This wisdom distinguishes outward and inward illumination, inviting care for guidance keeping the heart aware as external circumstances change.

Al-athar means traces of creation, while al-awsaf refers to Allah's attributes recognized through His guidance. Al-qulub wa al-sara'ir means hearts and inner depths. Shams al-qulub, the sun of hearts, portrays knowledge continually illuminating devotion's direction. Never setting expresses guidance's steadfastness rather than a human never tiring, grieving, or needing reminders.

Someone understanding honesty's importance retains a guide when workplace culture encourages deception. Someone knowing Allah's generosity can still hope when plans are delayed. That light appears in maintained decisions, without requiring special visual experiences. Sound knowledge and habits of obedience help the heart gain a steadier direction.

Care for inward illumination through learning, guided dhikr, and honest self-examination. When attention weakens, return to what is clear without feeling the entire journey lost. Seek help and advice if needed. This wisdom helps devotion avoid complete dependence on external comfort. Circumstances may alternate like day and night, while faith is trained as a light for our steps, helping us keep trusts in unsupportive conditions.
shortEn: Assalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh. Alhamdulillah, all praise belongs to Allah. May blessings and peace be upon Prophet Muhammad, his family, and his Companions.

Dear friends, when lights go out somewhere, things can change quickly. People seek each other, voices rise, and some panic. We need illumination to see the path. Yet life also needs another guidance: clarity about right actions. In difficulty, that guide remains necessary even when comfort and calm decrease.

Ibn 'Ata'illah distinguishes outward light from the heart's light. The sun may set while sound knowledge directs devotion. The sun-of-the-heart metaphor does not mean someone is always happy or never needs reminders. We understand guidance's steadfastness as continually nurtured, so external change does not automatically erase reasonably clear boundaries and responsibilities.

Dear congregation, when an activity suddenly becomes chaotic, protect vulnerable people's rights. Do not push others or take what is not yours. Give accurate information and follow safety directions. Character is tested in discomfort. Learned guidance needs to appear in small decisions beyond easy words when the room is bright and needs met.

“If I am afraid too, how can I calm others?” We need not be free of fear to choose responsibility. Focus attention on a clear step and seek help if needed. If unsure, ask someone able to guide. Do not spread guesses increasing panic. Acknowledging limits is better than giving baseless certainty.

Dear friends, inward light is nurtured through knowledge, guided worship, and honest self-examination. When attention weakens, learn again and receive reminders. We need not claim an unshakeable heart. Humility preserves room for guidance, allowing others to correct safely and helping us improve more quickly when steps begin harming people.

Let us seek illumination reaching action. May Allah protect in emergencies, strengthen character as comfort decreases, and help guard information and rights. May learned guidance remain nurtured, so changed external conditions still leave the heart reasons to choose rightly and hands ready to help those nearby. Amin.
Wassalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh.

Yet we are all still learning about holding to good character when comfort suddenly disappears. So let us not feel that we are too late for this discussion. Those who are older can still discover a new understanding, and children can still bring serious questions. Let us listen with an open heart. If an example does not match our circumstances exactly, notice the attitude being discussed. Often, beneath differences in work or age, there is a habit of the heart that many of us recognize.

Do not take one fragment of a sentence and use it to justify all our own wishes. Listen to it in full. Then test our understanding through a simple example. Lights go out in a crowded room. Several people stand simultaneously and voices rise. Dear friends, we may be afraid too but can still notice clear steps. Do not push, protect entrusted belongings, and listen to safety directions. Ask if unsure rather than spreading panic-provoking guesses. Vulnerable people may need space or company. Help within ability without creating new danger. Discomfort reveals learned guidance's importance because words about character need to appear when surroundings no longer support calm.

“What if I cannot calm myself?” We need not give every direction, dear congregation. Follow right steps and request help where needed. Admitting limits benefits more than baseless certainty. The sun of the heart portrays steady knowledge giving direction. It does not mean humans never fear or tire. Reminders and means remain necessary. Nurtured lessons can help choose actions before feelings are orderly. Therefore character is practised in ordinary circumstances too, making others' rights easier to recall during disruption.

Now try answering silently, dear friends: “What right step remains possible when we too feel afraid and confused?” There is no need to hurry. People may give different answers because their circumstances also differ. We listen while holding to the guidance that is already clear. If someone is new to learning, give them a chance to ask. If someone has made a mistake, do not make their experience a joke. A safe conversation gives us courage to examine our own habits. Then we can choose a reasonable improvement. May a gathering like this send us home with the courage to learn, rather than merely the ability to comment on other people's lives.
PERSONAL REFLECTION

The lesson about holding to good character when comfort suddenly disappears may touch an experience that is still unresolved. We do not have to force all our feelings into order tonight. Simply recognize one part that now seems clearer. Perhaps we need to apologize, seek an explanation, or change how we make decisions. Perhaps we first need rest so that we can think clearly. We can examine all of this calmly. Turn our attention towards an action we can manage today, then ask Allah for help with the next stage of the process.

Let us leave room for questions that remain unresolved, dear congregation. If confusion remains after the gathering, write down the issue clearly. Then ask someone who understands the subject and knows the circumstances involved. We may learn gradually. A little accurate understanding is more helpful than a rushed decision made simply because we want to feel that everything is settled. Meanwhile, continue fulfilling our clear obligations and respect the rights of those around us.

Seek help and advice if needed. This wisdom helps devotion avoid complete dependence on external comfort. Circumstances may alternate like day and night, while faith is trained as a light for our steps, helping us keep trusts in unsupportive conditions.

Try examining one habit when activities change suddenly. Do we seek information or immediately accuse? Practise asking the right person and conveying only what is known. Families can discuss safety needs without frightening stories. Do not mock those who panicked afterwards. May guidance retain a place in decisions and help us care for others as comfort decreases. We seek Allah's help so fear does not drag actions towards increased harm.

Let us arrange a step that fits our lives, dear congregation. The lesson about holding to good character when comfort suddenly disappears will be easier to remember when connected with a time or activity that already exists. We do not need to add burdens without considering our ability. Choose a reasonable place to begin, and respect other people's rights as we act. Children may ask for their parents' support; adults can also seek advice when struggling. We do not have to face everything alone. What we want to nurture is a willingness to do our part properly and in an orderly way, even when the results still take time to appear.

Dear congregation, try practising that answer in our own words. Imagine a family member asking while we are relaxing. We do not need to give a long sermon. Begin by listening, then share what we truly understand. If something remains unclear, say that we will learn more. A simple conversation like this helps us check our own understanding while ensuring that advice is given respectfully. We learn together, without needing to appear as people who have already resolved every problem.
REINFORCING THE MESSAGE AND CLOSING SUPPLICATION

Dear congregation, after hearing this explanation about holding to good character when comfort suddenly disappears, keep one insight that is closest to our circumstances. We can recall it on the journey home or discuss it with our family without talking down to them. Ask ourselves which part we have understood and which part needs further study. In this way, the conversation continues naturally beyond the gathering. We do not need to monitor other people's inner states. It is enough to care for the responsibilities already before us. May this little knowledge help us choose a step pleasing to Allah when we face the matter in real life.

Let us seek illumination reaching action. May Allah protect in emergencies, strengthen character as comfort decreases, and help guard information and rights. May learned guidance remain nurtured, so changed external conditions still leave the heart reasons to choose rightly and hands ready to help those nearby. Amin.
Wassalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh.
phrasesEn: أَنَارَ الظَّوَاهِرَ بِأَنْوَارِ آثَارِهِ،
He illuminates outward reality with the light of the traces of His creation.
وَأَنَارَ السَّرَائِرَ بِأَنْوَارِ أَوْصَافِهِ،
He illuminates inner secrets with the light of His attributes.
لِأَجْلِ ذَلِكَ أَفَلَتْ أَنْوَارُ الظَّوَاهِرِ وَلَمْ تَأْفُلْ أَنْوَارُ الْقُلُوبِ وَالسَّرَائِرِ،
Outward light can therefore set, while the light of hearts and inner secrets does not set.
وَلِذَلِكَ قِيلَ إِنَّ شَمْسَ النَّهَارِ تَغْرُبُ بِاللَّيْلِ
Thus it is said: the daytime sun sets at night,
وَشَمْسُ الْقُلُوبِ لَيْسَتْ تَغِيبُ.
but the sun of hearts never sets.

115.translation: Let the pain of your trial be eased by knowing that He, glorified is He, is the One testing you. The One sending the decrees of destiny to you is the One who has always chosen goodness for you.
syarahEn: Trials can narrow our view to present pain. We forget much sustaining care and help throughout life. This wisdom invites the heart to remember the One testing as the Lord who has also bestowed gifts, so difficulty does not extinguish all hope.

Al-bala' means trial, while al-mubtali refers to the One testing. Husn al-ikhtiyar describes the goodness of Allah's choice and arrangements for the servant. The words invite viewing trials within broader knowledge of Allah. We are not required to know every event's particular purpose, but invited to maintain trust while fulfilling clear responsibilities.

Someone losing an important opportunity may feel sad and need adjustment time. They can remember past help without forcing pain to disappear immediately. That memory gives strength to seek the next path, request assistance, and maintain obligations still possible.

This wisdom is best used first to strengthen ourselves. Supporting others, prioritize compassion, practical needs, and listening. Do not reduce suffering to hasty advice. Trust grows more healthily when feelings are acknowledged and efforts continue. We may ask for lighter trials and steadfastness to live through them. Remembering Allah's care beyond one event gives the heart room for hope without understanding the entire path.
shortEn: Assalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh. Alhamdulillah, all praise belongs to Allah. May blessings and peace be upon Prophet Muhammad, his family, and his Companions.

Dear congregation, losing someone loved can leave a formerly lively home very quiet. Small habits suddenly disappear: a calling voice, a seat, or a regular message. Hasty advice can feel heavy then. A grieving person may need no long explanation, only company and assistance with today's needs.

Ibn 'Ata'illah reminds a tested servant to recognize Allah's long sustaining care. Remembering His generosity can support a hurting heart. We bring this message compassionately. It does not demand sadness disappear immediately or make tears evidence of insufficient trust. We may grieve while hoping Allah's help accompanies the difficult process.

Dear friends, when visiting bereaved family, listen first. Do not force repeated accounts of the event. Ask concrete needs, perhaps food or household help. Offer supplication gently. A presence making few demands can mean much, especially after visitors decrease and family again faces long days.

“What if I am grieving?” Allow feelings and seek safe support. Strength does not require holding every tear. Continue bodily care and obligations according to guidance and ability. If the burden feels extremely heavy, request suitable help. Loved ones may want to assist but need to know what is truly needed.

Dear congregation, remembering Allah's kindness can happen slowly: perhaps through someone bringing food or a relative offering company. We need not force every loss to gain an immediately relieving explanation. Maintain one possible step, one expressible prayer, and one relationship helping us avoid prolonged solitude through every difficult day.

Let us pray for grieving families. May Allah have mercy on those returned to Him, strengthen those left, and guide wise companionship. May sadness have room without extinguishing hope. May remembering His care give strength to continue gradually, with compassion we can still receive and offer. Amin.
Wassalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh.

Dear congregation, may Allah honour us, before the inspiration of this lesson passes, let us choose a practical exercise about accompanying grief with undemanding attention. We do not all have to choose the same step. Our families, work, and abilities differ. What matters is that our choice follows the wisdom's message and respects the obligations we already have. Allow a reasonable time to try it. If a change affects others, listen to their views. We are learning to develop habits we can practise in real life. Advice then begins to shape how we handle our responsibilities, instead of remaining something we agree with during the gathering.

Dear friends, take a moment to connect this explanation with a decision we once made. If we could go through that experience again, what would we want to improve? Of course, we cannot turn back time. But what we learned can still help us face the next situation. Keep one clear lesson. If someone's rights still need to be fulfilled, consider a proper way to fulfil them. Reflection becomes useful when it helps us move forward in the life we are living now.
REINFORCING THE MESSAGE AND CLOSING SUPPLICATION

Dear friends, before we close, silently recall the lesson we most want to take home. Today we have spoken about accompanying grief with undemanding attention. We do not have to feel accomplished after a single meeting. A clearer understanding and a willingness to begin are enough. If we later forget, we can open our notes or ask again. Do not be embarrassed to repeat a good lesson. Life gives us opportunities to practise many times. May each repetition make our actions a little more orderly and our hearts more aware of our need for Allah's help. Let us keep that willingness to learn after leaving this gathering.

Let us pray for grieving families. May Allah have mercy on those returned to Him, strengthen those left, and guide wise companionship. May sadness have room without extinguishing hope. May remembering His care give strength to continue gradually, with compassion we can still receive and offer. Amin.
Wassalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh.
phrasesEn: لِيُخَفِّفْ عَنْكَ أَلَمَ الْبَلَاءِ عَلَيْكَ
Let the pain of your trial be eased
عِلْمُكَ بِأَنَّهُ سُبْحَانَهُ هُوَ الْمُبْتَلِي لَكَ،
by knowing that He, glorified is He, is the One testing you.
فَالَّذِي وَاجَهَتْكَ مِنْهُ الْأَقْدَارُ
The One sending the decrees of destiny to you
هُوَ الَّذِي عَوَّدَكَ حُسْنَ الِاخْتِيَارِ.
is the One who has always chosen goodness for you.

116.translation: Whoever supposes His gentleness separate from His decree does so because their vision is limited.
syarahEn: When difficulty arrives, we easily assume Allah's gentleness is absent. Yet human sight does not encompass the whole chain of causes and consequences. This wisdom invites us to avoid hastily separating Allah's decree from possible accompanying mercy, while remaining honest about the experience's weight.

Lutf means gentleness or subtle goodness, sometimes not immediately visible. Qadar refers to Allah's decree. Infikak means separation, while qusur nazarih describes limited sight. The sentence reminds us that judgement may come too quickly because we see only the painful part without knowing what else is unfolding.

Within difficulty, gentleness may be recognized through companions, endurance, or an opening for help. Yet we need not construct a story that every wound must immediately be replaced by a particular success. Some experiences require long periods and continual support. Admitting limited understanding is more honest than forcing an unknown conclusion.

Seek needed help and clear lessons. If injustice exists, pursue protection and accountability properly. Belief in destiny does not release people from those duties. This wisdom mainly guards the heart against closing every possibility of mercy in disappointment. We seek relief, improve circumstances, and allow room for Allah's help to arrive in forms not immediately recognized.
shortEn: Assalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh. Alhamdulillah, all praise belongs to Allah. May blessings and peace be upon Prophet Muhammad, his family, and his Companions.

Dear friends, may Allah honour us, amid heavy matters, small help can almost escape sight. While awaiting a relative's treatment, someone offers food. During a disrupted journey, someone provides accurate information. The main problem remains unresolved, but help makes part of the day more manageable. Goodness can coexist with circumstances still difficult and unclear.

Ibn 'Ata'illah recalls limited vision making someone imagine Allah's gentleness separate from His decree. We do not see life's whole sequence. The message opens room to recognize help without erasing difficulty's reality. We need not call suffering pleasant or force others to feel lighter because we have found one aspect deserving gratitude.

Dear congregation, those facing problems can notice available support. Who can help a particular task? What information needs seeking? Receive good assistance reasonably and express thanks. Needing others does not make us weak. Sometimes continued effort opens when we stop carrying everything alone and share responsibly.

“What if I see no help yet?” We may be honest. Seek help properly and continue expressing needs. We need not invent conclusions to sound steadfast. Some problems require time and specialized attention. If mistreatment is involved, pursue suitable protection and responsibility. Faith in Allah accompanies reducing harm and protecting human safety.

Dear friends, we can become part of small assistance too. Do not wait until able to solve someone's entire problem. Ask one task you can take and fulfil it earnestly. Avoid oversized promises. Simple reliable help is often more useful than impressive words never followed through when support is truly needed.

Let us seek clear sight and willing hands. May Allah protect those tested, bring suitable assistance, and strengthen continued effort. May present goodness be recognized without belittling wounds. May we appreciate blessings while seeking safer, fairer, and better circumstances for others. Amin.
Wassalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh.

Assalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh. Alhamdulillah, all praise belongs to Allah. May blessings and peace be upon Prophet Muhammad, his family, and his Companions.

Dear congregation, may Allah have mercy on us, imagine taking this reminder home with us. We have taken off our shoes, the gathering is over, and ordinary life begins again. That is where the lesson about receiving small help while a large problem continues will be tested. We may still face the same situation, the same people, and old habits that have not yet changed. We need to understand the message well enough to bring it into those circumstances. Listen slowly. If a sentence speaks to our situation, keep it in mind for later. We do not have to remember every explanation. One sound understanding, put sincerely into practice, is already worth working towards today.
CORE WISDOM

The sentence reminds us that judgement may come too quickly because we see only the painful part without knowing what else is unfolding.

Dear friends, after hearing that explanation, give our minds room to connect its meaning with actual events. We need not use the lesson about receiving small help while a large problem continues as a label for judging people's inner states. We see only part of their lives. For ourselves, this advice can become an honest question. What am I hoping for? What am I neglecting? Our answer may not be complete today. That is all right. What matters is being willing to learn sincerely, examine our understanding, and follow sound guidance when seeking to change our daily habits.
EXAMPLES AND CONVERSATION WITH THE CONGREGATION

Dear congregation, those facing problems can notice available support. Who can help a particular task? What information needs seeking? Receive good assistance reasonably and express thanks. Needing others does not make us weak. Sometimes continued effort opens when we stop carrying everything alone and share responsibly.

“What if I see no help yet?” We may be honest. Seek help properly and continue expressing needs. We need not invent conclusions to sound steadfast. Some problems require time and specialized attention. If mistreatment is involved, pursue suitable protection and responsibility. Faith in Allah accompanies reducing harm and protecting human safety.

In a waiting room, someone is exhausted worrying about family. A neighbour brings food and offers to take over briefly. The main problem remains, but one need receives attention. Dear friends, we may accept help without feeling obliged to be happy about everything. Arriving goodness does not erase fear. It simply eases one part. We may give thanks and name other appropriate needs. Accepting assistance opens cooperation, so one person does not keep carrying every task merely to appear able to endure alone.

“What if I see no help at all?” We may be honest, dear congregation. Do not invent a story to seem steadfast. Seek help properly and state needs clearly. If mistreatment exists, pursue protection and responsibility. The wisdom about Allah's gentleness reminds us of limited sight rather than justifying blindness to actual harm. We may not know everything unfolding. Meanwhile, clear steps remain. Supporters can help practically without forcing those struggling immediately to call every circumstance easy to accept.

Dear friends, if we sat in a circle after the lesson, someone might raise this question: “Has one part of the day become more manageable through another person's help?” That question deserves to be heard. We should not rush to answer before understanding the difficulty. We can begin by restating the issue in simple language, then consider the available choices. If we do not know the whole answer, we can admit it and continue learning. What matters is that the conversation leads towards a good action. Now think about the answer we would give a friend. Choose words that are clear and gentle, without promising an outcome beyond human ability.
PERSONAL REFLECTION

Within difficulty, gentleness may be recognized through companions, endurance, or an opening for help. Yet we need not construct a story that every wound must immediately be replaced by a particular success. Some experiences require long periods and continual support. Admitting limited understanding is more honest than forcing an unknown conclusion.

Dear friends, we can become part of small assistance too. Do not wait until able to solve someone's entire problem. Ask one task you can take and fulfil it earnestly. Avoid oversized promises. Simple reliable help is often more useful than impressive words never followed through when support is truly needed.

Dear friends, before moving to practical steps, let us give ourselves room to absorb this. The lesson about receiving small help while a large problem continues may touch an experience that is still unresolved. We do not have to force all our feelings into order tonight. Simply recognize one part that now seems clearer. Perhaps we need to apologize, seek an explanation, or change how we make decisions. Perhaps we first need rest so that we can think clearly. We can examine all of this calmly. Turn our attention towards an action we can manage today, then ask Allah for help with the next stage of the process.

Dear friends, take a moment to connect this explanation with a decision we once made. If we could go through that experience again, what would we want to improve? Of course, we cannot turn back time. But what we learned can still help us face the next situation. Keep one clear lesson. If someone's rights still need to be fulfilled, consider a proper way to fulfil them. Reflection becomes useful when it helps us move forward in the life we are living now.
PRACTICAL STEPS TO TRY

Seek needed help and clear lessons. If injustice exists, pursue protection and accountability properly. Belief in destiny does not release people from those duties. This wisdom mainly guards the heart against closing every possibility of mercy in disappointment. We seek relief, improve circumstances, and allow room for Allah's help to arrive in forms not immediately recognized.

For practice, identify one shareable task and someone who might help. Ask respectfully and allow room to state ability. Helpers should offer clear assistance and fulfil commitments. Avoid demanding stories or praise from recipients. May small help support an unfinished journey, and may the heart grow braver in acknowledging need for Allah and receiving good means. We keep hoping while seeking actions protecting safety and reducing burdens within ability.

Now let us turn the lesson about receiving small help while a large problem continues into a simple plan, dear friends. Choose one action with a reasonably clear time for doing it. Do not immediately promise to change our whole life. Ask when we can begin and what needs preparing. If other people are involved, speak with them properly; do not make decisions on their behalf in a passing burst of enthusiasm. After trying, notice what helped and what still got in the way. We may adjust our approach while keeping the right aim. A small exercise gives us a chance to learn from real circumstances, so a good intention takes a form we can actually carry out.

Dear congregation, if we wish to respond, sharing the general lesson is enough. We do not need to name anyone or reveal anybody's private affairs. Listen calmly to different responses. There may be circumstances we have never considered. After listening, return to the message we are studying and consider the most appropriate action. Learning together can broaden our understanding, provided the conversation respects people's dignity and does not become a place for judging their experiences.
REINFORCING THE MESSAGE AND CLOSING SUPPLICATION

Let us recall the direction of today's discussion, dear congregation. The lesson about receiving small help while a large problem continues invites us to examine our own choices and improve what is our responsibility. After returning home, things may feel ordinary again. That is where a good intention needs attention. We can remind ourselves gently while remaining firm about our obligations. If we need to begin again one day, let us begin. The opportunity to learn is not exhausted because one attempt has not gone smoothly. While we have the ability and opportunity, let us keep seeking goodness and asking Allah to guide our hearts and accept our deeds.

Let us seek clear sight and willing hands. May Allah protect those tested, bring suitable assistance, and strengthen continued effort. May present goodness be recognized without belittling wounds. May we appreciate blessings while seeking safer, fairer, and better circumstances for others. Amin.
Wassalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh.
phrasesEn: مَنْ ظَنَّ انْفِكَاكَ لُطْفِهِ عَنْ قَدَرِهِ
Whoever supposes His gentleness separate from His decree
فَذَلِكَ لِقُصُورِ نَظَرِهِ.
does so because their vision is limited.

117.translation: The concern is not merely that the path is unclear to you. The greater concern is that desire dominates you.
syarahEn: Confusion does not always arise because goodness's path is unclear. Sometimes guidance is known but desire seeks reasons to avoid it. We know honesty is needed but fear losing profit. This wisdom invites greater watchfulness against desire's domination than merely feeling short of information about the right path.

Taltabisa al-turuq means paths becoming unclear or mixed. Ghalabat al-hawa refers to desire's force dominating decisions. Yukhafu means feared or a matter of concern. The emphasis is desire's direction: even clear information can be twisted if we accept only explanations justifying our own choice.

For example, someone repeatedly seeks advice about a financial trust but rejects every answer requiring openness. They seek more opinions until finding one suited to preference. More questions may not solve the issue then. What needs examination is willingness to accept consequences of truth already understood.

Learning and asking remain important when something genuinely is unclear. Choose knowledgeable, trustworthy people, explain circumstances fully, and allow unwelcome answers. Delay decisions when emotions are too strong, then examine calmly. This wisdom teaches honesty about inner impulses. We ask guidance beyond knowing direction: we need courage to follow. Knowledge benefits when the heart accepts guidance rather than continually using reasons to protect dominating desires.
shortEn: Assalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh. Alhamdulillah, all praise belongs to Allah. May blessings and peace be upon Prophet Muhammad, his family, and his Companions.

Dear congregation, have we asked someone a question and received an unwanted answer? We ask another. If the answer is similar, we keep searching until finding the easiest for our plan. Asking is good, but honesty is needed: are we seeking guidance, or collecting reasons to make a desired decision feel permissible and beyond further examination?

Ibn 'Ata'illah warns that the greater concern is more than an unclear path: it is desire dominating choices. Information may be clear enough, but wanting makes us turn away. This wisdom invites examination of questions' direction. We still learn carefully, including differences of opinion, while guarding against personal desire quietly determining every answer considered worth hearing.

Dear friends, suppose we hold entrusted money and want to use it briefly without permission. The heart already knows someone has rights to protect. Yet we seek stories that others do it too. Their habit does not automatically resolve the trust. The clearer step is requesting permission or refraining rather than continually finding reasons to ignore the owner's right to know how money is used.

“What if opinions genuinely differ?” Learn from competent people, explain circumstances fully, and ask about basis and application. Do not conceal important details to obtain the desired answer. Honesty in asking helps obtain proper guidance. We need not master every discussion, but must be willing to hear explanations perhaps requiring changed plans.

Dear congregation, when an answer provokes resistance, allow time before deciding. Ask what we fear losing: perhaps comfort, profit, or recognition. Recognizing desire helps order choices. If needed, ask a trustworthy friend to think alongside you. Do not choose only someone always agreeing, because we need clarity beyond momentary comfort from unanimous approval.

Let us seek guidance and willingness to follow. May Allah protect against bending knowledge for desire, grant honesty in questions, and help respect rights. May learning improve steps even when answers disappoint. May we receive courage to change plans when a desired method must be left to preserve a trust. Amin.
Wassalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh.

Dear congregation, let us settle into a comfortable atmosphere for learning. Talking about asking to receive guidance rather than merely justification calls for honesty, but that honesty can remain quietly within the heart. We are under no obligation to share private affairs before everyone. Simply listen, consider, and identify what can be improved. Sometimes we already know the advice, but have not made time to think about it. This gathering gives us that opportunity. We can revisit a sound understanding until it becomes clearer. Afterwards, when we face everyday situations, may we have words that help us choose our actions more calmly and responsibly.

Dear friends, we may appreciate the beautiful words in a saying of wisdom. Still, let us make time to understand what they mean. In discussing asking to receive guidance rather than merely justification, a word's meaning needs to be considered alongside the circumstances being addressed. Do not take one fragment of a sentence and use it to justify all our own wishes. Listen to it in full. Then test our understanding through a simple example. Does this explanation make our responsibilities clearer? Are other people's rights still protected? Questions like these help us read advice with a humble heart and a mind willing to learn.
EXAMPLES AND CONVERSATION WITH THE CONGREGATION

Dear friends, suppose we hold entrusted money and want to use it briefly without permission. The heart already knows someone has rights to protect. Yet we seek stories that others do it too. Honesty in asking helps obtain proper guidance. We need not master every discussion, but must be willing to hear explanations perhaps requiring changed plans.

We want to use entrusted money briefly. When asking, we deliberately omit that the owner has given no permission. The answer then seems to support the plan. Dear friends, incomplete questions can produce explanations unsuited to reality. Share decisive details with competent people. Do not use answers as shields for actions already desired. More clearly, ask the owner's permission or refrain. A trust concerns their right to know use of their property. Strong desire needs honesty, including when advice may require abandoning something already hoped for.

“If opinions differ, may I seek another explanation?” Further learning is allowed, dear congregation. Ask competent people and explain circumstances fully. Distinguish understanding basis and application from moving around until finding the most pleasing answer. This wisdom recalls desire dominating decisions can obscure a sufficiently clear path. Knowledge remains needed, but the heart's acceptance needs examination too. More information brings little benefit when every part requiring responsibility is immediately discarded. Honest questions help guidance find its proper place.

Let me ask a question, dear congregation: “Have we honestly shared important details with the person advising us?” Take a moment to think about it. Perhaps an answer comes straight away; perhaps a difficulty comes to mind instead. Let us hear that difficulty calmly. Good advice needs to meet the reality of life, including the limitations we face. Now imagine someone we love asking that question. Would our answer help them act, or simply leave them feeling scolded? Here we learn to convey the truth in a way that can be received. We also need honesty that gives direction when speaking to ourselves, so that understanding a problem gives us courage to begin putting it right.
PERSONAL REFLECTION

For example, someone repeatedly seeks advice about a financial trust but rejects every answer requiring openness. They seek more opinions until finding one suited to preference. More questions may not solve the issue then. What needs examination is willingness to accept consequences of truth already understood.

If needed, ask a trustworthy friend to think alongside you. Do not choose only someone always agreeing, because we need clarity beyond momentary comfort from unanimous approval.

Dear congregation, try looking at our own journey with both honesty and compassion. In the matter of asking to receive guidance rather than merely justification, we may have made small progress for which we have never given thanks. There may also be a mistake we keep wanting to hide. Both can teach us without being put on display. Give thanks for the help that has already come, then examine what needs improving. Do not compare our whole journey with a fragment of someone else's life. We have real responsibilities today. Recognizing our part allows reflection to move into action, so regret need not remain a thought circling endlessly without direction.

Dear congregation, if we wish to respond, sharing the general lesson is enough. We do not need to name anyone or reveal anybody's private affairs. Listen calmly to different responses. There may be circumstances we have never considered. After listening, return to the message we are studying and consider the most appropriate action. Learning together can broaden our understanding, provided the conversation respects people's dignity and does not become a place for judging their experiences.
PRACTICAL STEPS TO TRY

Learning and asking remain important when something genuinely is unclear. Choose knowledgeable, trustworthy people, explain circumstances fully, and allow unwelcome answers. Delay decisions when emotions are too strong, then examine calmly. This wisdom teaches honesty about inner impulses. We ask guidance beyond knowing direction: we need courage to follow. Knowledge benefits when the heart accepts guidance rather than continually using reasons to protect dominating desires.

For practice, take an issue on which advice is being sought. Write important facts separately from personal wants. When asking, omit nothing that could change judgement. If an answer is unclear, politely seek explanation rather than immediate alternative justification. Advisers may also ask to confirm circumstances and acknowledge limits. May desire for guidance exceed the need to defend a plan, and may decisions preserving trusts arise from honest understanding.

Dear congregation, if we want to take one task home from this discussion of asking to receive guidance rather than merely justification, choose something we can truly do. There is no need to announce it now. We can decide after getting home, when we have a fuller picture of our circumstances. Make the step small enough for us to know when it will be done. If there are obstacles, consider what reasonable help we need. We may also ask a trusted person to remind us respectfully. Change requires our involvement, as well as a heart that feels inspired. Let us accompany a good intention with preparation that makes it easier to carry out.

Dear friends, we can pause before answering a question that feels close to home. Sometimes our first answer comes from a habit of defending ourselves. Given time, we can hear the advice more clearly. We do not have to make everyone speak immediately. Some people think more easily in silence, while others are helped by asking questions. What matters is making room to understand, then choosing a step sincerely. We want to learn in a way that preserves good manners and makes our responsibilities clearer.
REINFORCING THE MESSAGE AND CLOSING SUPPLICATION

Dear friends, our problems may not be resolved immediately after this lesson. Yet may we gain a clearer way of seeing the matter of asking to receive guidance rather than merely justification. That clarity can help us take the next step more responsibly. Carry a sound understanding, then make room for the process of learning. If help is needed, seek it properly. If we can already begin, act without waiting for every circumstance to become perfect. We have an opportunity to make an effort today, and we continue asking Allah for help. With that hope, let us bring this meeting to a close with supplication and a willingness to put the lesson into practice.

Let us seek guidance and willingness to follow. May Allah protect against bending knowledge for desire, grant honesty in questions, and help respect rights. May learning improve steps even when answers disappoint. May we receive courage to change plans when a desired method must be left to preserve a trust. Amin.
Wassalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh.
phrasesEn: لَا يُخَافُ عَلَيْكَ أَنْ تَلْتَبِسَ الطُّرُقُ عَلَيْكَ،
The concern is not merely that the path is unclear to you.
وَإِنَّمَا يُخَافُ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ غَلَبَةِ الْهَوَى عَلَيْكَ.
The greater concern is desire dominating you.

118.translation: Glorified is the One who conceals the secret of special distinction beneath ordinary human appearance, and manifests the majesty of His Lordship through the realization of servanthood.
syarahEn: Those close to Allah still live as human beings. They eat, work, tire, and may appear simple. This wisdom warns against judging devotion's depth solely by outward impression. Distinction can be hidden behind daily life attracting little attention.

Al-khususiyyah means special distinction or a distinctive gift. Al-bashariyyah refers to visible human qualities. Al-rububiyyah concerns Allah's Lordship and sustaining care, while al-'ubudiyyah means servanthood. Allah's majesty is known through a servant's obedience and need for Him. The sentence does not deify a human; the servant's position reveals their Lord's power and generosity.

Someone patiently caring for family can show devotion's quality without followers. A humble teacher can convey knowledge without creating an impression of extraordinary powers. We should respect practical goodness while assessing behaviour through religious guidance. Neither simple nor imposing appearances give certainty about inner standing.

For yourself, do not chase signs of distinction to feel valuable. Fulfil proper duties and care for intention within them. If influential, do not demand unquestioned acceptance of every action. Closeness to Allah does not remove human responsibility. This wisdom helps humility towards ourselves and fairness towards others. We appreciate quiet service and remember a servant's honour grows in submission rather than demands for treatment beyond human limits.
shortEn: Assalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh. Alhamdulillah, all praise belongs to Allah. May blessings and peace be upon Prophet Muhammad, his family, and his Companions.

Dear friends, may Allah have mercy on us, some people are rarely named although their work enables many activities. They open doors, arrange chairs, or ensure rooms are ready. Appearance is ordinary and speech simple. Without visible distinction, we easily pass without greeting. Yet service benefiting us often rests on work outside the centre of attention.

Ibn 'Ata'illah reminds us that distinction can be concealed beneath ordinary humanity. A servant remains human with needs and limits. We are not tasked with determining special ranks. The accessible lesson is to stop measuring devotion solely by outward impressions while continuing to assess conduct through guidance and responsibilities known in everyday interaction.

Dear congregation, closeness to Allah need not appear as extraordinary public ability. Nor should we attach such claims to anyone without basis. Better to respect practical goodness. Pay workers' rights, hear needs, and do not make service a reason to expect constant availability without rest or room for concerns.

“What if I want to benefit others without being known?” Begin with available needs. Work orderly, learn what exceeds ability, and protect rights. A known name is not every benefit's condition. If work needs publicity so people know whom to contact, do so honestly. Guard the purpose so service does not continually await attention before beginning.

Dear friends, invite children to recognize helpers. Name them if known and give thanks. Do more than introduce people holding office. Children learn human respect through whom we greet and how we speak. This small habit can create greater equality, ensuring quiet work still receives fitting appreciation.

Let us notice again those long easing our steps. May Allah bless their service, provide family needs, and protect against degrading treatment. May our hearts avoid being dazzled by appearances or quick feelings of superiority. May practical goodness remain respected even through hands of simple people rarely mentioned in praise. Amin.
Wassalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh.

We may arrive with questions, with experiences we have not yet worked through, and even with confusion. In this gathering we learn together. I, too, need to practise what I share. Dear congregation, a saying of wisdom may be very short, yet reflection reveals how deeply it touches our long-standing habits. We are seeing that here in the matter of respecting the service that enables activities. Its brevity should not make us feel that we have finished understanding it. Try expressing its meaning again in our own words. If it still seems unclear, return to the earlier example. We are not competing to memorize terminology. We want guidance we can use. In this way, a word that once sounded unfamiliar can help us recognize a mistaken step before the habit makes life harder for us or for others.
EXAMPLES AND CONVERSATION WITH THE CONGREGATION

Doors are open and chairs arranged as the congregation enters. Afterwards, some leave without noticing those tidying again. Dear friends, greet and offer appropriate appreciation. If service is employment carrying rights, fulfil them responsibly. Do not replace obligations with praise for sincerity. Rest and room to state needs matter too. Felt benefit comes through real energy. Simple appearance does not make workers permanently available. We learn respect without awaiting publicly striking stories of special distinction.

“If I want to help without being known, where do I begin?” Look at available needs and abilities, dear congregation. Learn proper methods and work orderly. If a responsible person's name needs clarity, state it honestly so people know whom to contact. Being known is not always something to avoid; purpose needs care. This wisdom about distinction appearing through humanity does not deify a servant or permit baseless claims. We respect visible goodness and acknowledge Allah's power granting servants ability without removing the distinction between Creator and creation.

Dear congregation, some questions look simple, but we only feel their weight when living through them: “Who prepared the venue before we arrived, and have their rights received attention?” Let us give ourselves time to consider this. We may picture ourselves or someone who needs support. We are learning to answer in words that can be put into practice. Avoid an answer that makes every problem seem resolved in a single breath. Some matters need time and support. Even so, that process can begin with a small decision. Try finding that decision in the earlier example. This is where our conversation becomes useful for life after the gathering ends.
PERSONAL REFLECTION

Someone patiently caring for family can show devotion's quality without followers. A humble teacher can convey knowledge without creating an impression of extraordinary powers. We should respect practical goodness while assessing behaviour through religious guidance. Neither simple nor imposing appearances give certainty about inner standing.

Dear friends, invite children to recognize helpers. Name them if known and give thanks. Do more than introduce people holding office. Children learn human respect through whom we greet and how we speak. This small habit can create greater equality, ensuring quiet work still receives fitting appreciation.

Dear friends, before moving to practical steps, let us give ourselves room to absorb this. The lesson about respecting the service that enables activities may touch an experience that is still unresolved. We do not have to force all our feelings into order tonight. Simply recognize one part that now seems clearer. Perhaps we need to apologize, seek an explanation, or change how we make decisions. Perhaps we first need rest so that we can think clearly. We can examine all of this calmly. Turn our attention towards an action we can manage today, then ask Allah for help with the next stage of the process.

Dear friends, we can pause before answering a question that feels close to home. Sometimes our first answer comes from a habit of defending ourselves. Given time, we can hear the advice more clearly. We do not have to make everyone speak immediately. Some people think more easily in silence, while others are helped by asking questions. What matters is making room to understand, then choosing a step sincerely. We want to learn in a way that preserves good manners and makes our responsibilities clearer.
PRACTICAL STEPS TO TRY

For yourself, do not chase signs of distinction to feel valuable. Fulfil proper duties and care for intention within them. If influential, do not demand unquestioned acceptance of every action. Closeness to Allah does not remove human responsibility. This wisdom helps humility towards ourselves and fairness towards others. We appreciate quiet service and remember a servant's honour grows in submission rather than demands for treatment beyond human limits.

At the next activity, notice one usually overlooked supporting task. Ask what help is appropriate before taking over. Follow venue rules so personal neglect does not add work. Managers can review task sharing and helpers' rights. Those doing simple tasks should maintain quality and ability limits without awaiting praise. May benefit grow through trustworthy work, and may respect become easier through rights and practical service even when someone's name is rarely mentioned.

Dear friends, test our plan against everyday situations. When we face the matter of respecting the service that enables activities again, what will change in our actions? Choose an answer we can recognize, such as having a conversation or stopping a habit. If the answer is still too general, make the step smaller. We are not writing a beautiful promise for others. We are preparing help for ourselves when we encounter an old habit. After doing it, give thanks and keep learning. If it has not worked yet, examine the reason honestly, then try again with preparation better suited to the situation.

Let us leave room for questions that remain unresolved, dear congregation. If confusion remains after the gathering, write down the issue clearly. Then ask someone who understands the subject and knows the circumstances involved. We may learn gradually. A little accurate understanding is more helpful than a rushed decision made simply because we want to feel that everything is settled. Meanwhile, continue fulfilling our clear obligations and respect the rights of those around us.
REINFORCING THE MESSAGE AND CLOSING SUPPLICATION

Dear friends, before we close, silently recall the lesson we most want to take home. Today we have spoken about respecting the service that enables activities. We do not have to feel accomplished after a single meeting. A clearer understanding and a willingness to begin are enough. If we later forget, we can open our notes or ask again. Do not be embarrassed to repeat a good lesson. Life gives us opportunities to practise many times. May each repetition make our actions a little more orderly and our hearts more aware of our need for Allah's help. Let us keep that willingness to learn after leaving this gathering.

Let us notice again those long easing our steps. May Allah bless their service, provide family needs, and protect against degrading treatment. May our hearts avoid being dazzled by appearances or quick feelings of superiority. May practical goodness remain respected even through hands of simple people rarely mentioned in praise. Amin.
Wassalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh.
phrasesEn: سُبْحَانَ مَنْ سَتَرَ سِرَّ الْخُصُوصِيَّةِ بِظُهُورِ الْبَشَرِيَّةِ،
Glorified is the One concealing the secret of distinction beneath ordinary human appearance,
وَظَهَرَ بِعَظَمَةِ الرُّبُوبِيَّةِ فِي إِظْهَارِ الْعُبُودِيَّةِ.
and manifesting His Lordship's majesty through the realization of servanthood.

119.translation: Do not demand of your Lord because your request remains unanswered. Demand of yourself because your manners towards Him still lag behind.
syarahEn: When a request remains unfulfilled, the heart can shift from asking to demanding. We count time as though Allah must follow our schedule. This wisdom returns attention to the servant's work: maintaining manners, examining efforts, and remaining humble before unwanted results.

La tutalib rabbaka means do not make demands of your Lord. Matlabuka refers to what is requested, while adabuka means your manners towards Him. The repeated demand is redirected to oneself. We are invited to examine responses and obligations more earnestly rather than constantly demand changes beyond our power.

For example, someone seeks abundant provision while continuing workplace deception. The needed improvement is clear without waiting for an answered prayer. Elsewhere, someone has tried properly and still waits. They must not conclude every delay results from inadequate manners. This wisdom is a mirror for improvement rather than a formula guessing every difficulty's cause.

Bring disappointment honestly into supplication, then guard inner language against accusing Allah. Ask what steps remain possible and whose rights remain unfulfilled. Seek goodness according to need while asking for help to accept His choice. Proper manners do not mean hiding sadness or forbidding hope. They order asking so relationship stays alive. Waiting can then contain practical responsibility, allowing supplication to strengthen devotion without becoming an attempt to force God's will.
shortEn: Assalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh. Alhamdulillah, all praise belongs to Allah. May blessings and peace be upon Prophet Muhammad, his family, and his Companions.

Dear congregation, when requests remain unfulfilled, we sometimes count waiting carefully: how long we have prayed and how many activities attended. But are we equally attentive to promises unfulfilled towards people? Some rights remain delayed and words unguarded. The heart demands external change while personal duties lack equal daily attention.

Ibn 'Ata'illah invites examination of delayed manners rather than continual demands for answers. We may still ask earnestly. We order attitude so prayer does not become a bill requiring Allah to follow our schedule. This wisdom is a personal mirror rather than a formula concluding everyone awaiting fulfilment must have bad manners or a particular fault.

Dear friends, suppose we pray for improved family relationships but still refuse to hear a spouse's explanation. Some steps can accompany prayer. Choose calm conversation time, acknowledge personal mistakes, and seek help if discussion keeps hurting. We do not control everyone's response, but can take responsibility for our presence and stop actions clearly worsening the relationship.

“What if I have tried improving but things remain unchanged?” We may feel disappointed and keep seeking proper paths. Improved manners do not force results. Others' choices and circumstances exceed our control. If safety or violated rights are involved, pursue protection. Patience accompanies responsible effort rather than an obligation to allow unlimited mistreatment.

Dear congregation, before repeating your most frequent request, identify one unfulfilled duty. No need to search for unknown faults. Examine what is clear: words, promises, or trusts. Choose reasonable improvement. Waiting then contains practical devotion, giving the heart good work beyond circling around disappointing unreceived results.

Let us ask with broad hope and continually improved manners. May Allah grant goodness, calm waiting hearts, and help fulfil duties. May prayer make self-examination more honest and treatment of others gentler. May what remains unfulfilled not block obedient steps still possible earnestly today. Amin.
Wassalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh.

Yet we are all still learning about examining manners while awaiting answered prayer. So let us not feel that we are too late for this discussion. Those who are older can still discover a new understanding, and children can still bring serious questions. Let us listen with an open heart. If an example does not match our circumstances exactly, notice the attitude being discussed. Often, beneath differences in work or age, there is a habit of the heart that many of us recognize.

Dear friends, after hearing that explanation, give our minds room to connect its meaning with actual events. We need not use the lesson about examining manners while awaiting answered prayer as a label for judging people's inner states. We see only part of their lives. For ourselves, this advice can become an honest question. What am I hoping for? What am I neglecting? Our answer may not be complete today. That is all right. What matters is being willing to learn sincerely, examine our understanding, and follow sound guidance when seeking to change our daily habits.
EXAMPLES AND CONVERSATION WITH THE CONGREGATION

We pray for an improved relationship, yet interrupt our spouse's explanation immediately. After failed conversation, we again ask why things have not changed. Dear friends, some things can be examined without controlling others' responses. Choose calm timing and hear them fully. Acknowledge hurtful words. If conversation is unsafe, seek suitable support. Prayer continues while clearly damaging actions stop. We do not let waiting excuse neglected personal duties. Improvement can begin with more responsible presence.

“What if I have changed but the other person has not?” We cannot control every choice, dear congregation. Keep seeking proper paths and safety. Manners do not force results on a schedule. This wisdom redirects careful demands towards our duties rather than forbidding requests in prayer. We may acknowledge disappointment and seek guidance. If rights are violated, pursue protection and resolution. Do not use this advice to burden the person most willing to yield with every problem. Self-examination accompanies fair assessment of everyone's actions.

Now try answering silently, dear friends: “What personal action can improve while we ask for changed circumstances?” There is no need to hurry. People may give different answers because their circumstances also differ. We listen while holding to the guidance that is already clear. If someone is new to learning, give them a chance to ask. If someone has made a mistake, do not make their experience a joke. A safe conversation gives us courage to examine our own habits. Then we can choose a reasonable improvement. May a gathering like this send us home with the courage to learn, rather than merely the ability to comment on other people's lives.

Dear congregation, try looking at our own journey with both honesty and compassion. In the matter of examining manners while awaiting answered prayer, we may have made small progress for which we have never given thanks. There may also be a mistake we keep wanting to hide. Both can teach us without being put on display. Give thanks for the help that has already come, then examine what needs improving. Do not compare our whole journey with a fragment of someone else's life. We have real responsibilities today. Recognizing our part allows reflection to move into action, so regret need not remain a thought circling endlessly without direction.

Let us leave room for questions that remain unresolved, dear congregation. If confusion remains after the gathering, write down the issue clearly. Then ask someone who understands the subject and knows the circumstances involved. We may learn gradually. For practice, choose a repeated request and a connected personal action. Examine what can already improve. If help is needed, seek someone understanding circumstances rather than quick to blame. Continue asking goodness without demanding uncontrollable certainty. May waiting become opportunity for good manners and fulfilled rights, and may we receive steadfastness in right steps before results match hopes. Allah knows efforts people may not see.

Let us arrange a step that fits our lives, dear congregation. The lesson about examining manners while awaiting answered prayer will be easier to remember when connected with a time or activity that already exists. We do not need to add burdens without considering our ability. Choose a reasonable place to begin, and respect other people's rights as we act. Children may ask for their parents' support; adults can also seek advice when struggling. We do not have to face everything alone. What we want to nurture is a willingness to do our part properly and in an orderly way, even when the results still take time to appear.

Dear congregation, try practising that answer in our own words. Imagine a family member asking while we are relaxing. We do not need to give a long sermon. Begin by listening, then share what we truly understand. If something remains unclear, say that we will learn more. A simple conversation like this helps us check our own understanding while ensuring that advice is given respectfully. We learn together, without needing to appear as people who have already resolved every problem.
REINFORCING THE MESSAGE AND CLOSING SUPPLICATION

Dear congregation, may Allah have mercy on us, choose one sentence from our discussion of examining manners while awaiting answered prayer that we want to remember tomorrow. Repeat its meaning silently in our own words. We do not need the sentence that sounds most impressive. Choose what helps most when facing real circumstances. Then ask Allah to enable us to put it into practice. We also pray for those struggling in similar circumstances. May this gathering make us more willing to support others with understanding while continuing to improve our own actions. Let us close this lesson with good hope and sincere supplication.

Let us ask with broad hope and continually improved manners. May Allah grant goodness, calm waiting hearts, and help fulfil duties. May prayer make self-examination more honest and treatment of others gentler. May what remains unfulfilled not block obedient steps still possible earnestly today. Amin.
Wassalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh.
phrasesEn: لَا تُطَالِبْ رَبَّكَ بِتَأَخُّرِ مَطْلَبِكَ،
Do not demand of your Lord because your request remains unanswered.
وَلَكِنْ طَالِبْ نَفْسَكَ بِتَأَخُّرِ أَدَبِكَ.
Demand of yourself because your manners towards Him still lag behind.

120.translation: When He makes your outward self obedient to His command and grants your inward self surrender to His power, He has indeed bestowed a great favour upon you.
syarahEn: Some fulfil obligations while their hearts continually argue with reality. Others speak of surrender while neglecting necessary duties. This wisdom shows a fuller gift: action following Allah's commands with a heart learning to accept limits and His decree.

Mumtathilan li-amrih means obedient to His command. Al-istislam refers to surrender or submission. Qahruhu means Allah's absolute power, while al-minnah means great favour. Outward and inward selves receive complementary work: the body follows guidance while the heart does not feel entitled to control every result.

Someone facing livelihood problems still works, seeks information, and improves skills. Meanwhile, they try to stop tormenting themselves with demands that results must arrive through one route. Someone supporting family also fulfils rights while accepting that every change cannot be accelerated according to their wishes.

Surrender is no reason to allow injustice or stop seeking help. Allah's commands include pursuing right through good means. We release claims to control results rather than duties to act. Practise both within one trust today: fulfil the clear part and entrust what exceeds ability through prayer. This wisdom helps life become more harmonious, so effort is not filled with arrogance and acceptance does not become laziness. We serve with available strength while continually needing Allah's help.
shortEn: Assalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh. Alhamdulillah, all praise belongs to Allah. May blessings and peace be upon Prophet Muhammad, his family, and his Companions.

Dear friends, may Allah honour us, as rainy season approaches, families in vulnerable areas need attention to circumstances. Some belongings need safe storage and information needs following. We naturally pray for protection. That supplication can accompany orderly preparation. The heart learns surrender while hands perform tasks helping protect those entrusted to us.

Ibn 'Ata'illah describes the great gift of an outward self helped to obey and an inward self granted surrender to Allah's power. They complement one another. We act according to guidance and ability without claiming certainty over every result. Surrender does not erase duties, and earnest effort gives no absolute power over coming events.

Dear congregation, heed warnings from authorized bodies and follow directions suited to local conditions. Discuss family needs, especially children, elders, and those requiring particular help. Do not await widespread panic before seeking information. We need not solve everything at once, but can undertake clear steps and ensure relatives know whom to contact when needed.

“What if preparation still does not prevent disaster?” We must not immediately blame victims or judge their faith. Much exceeds human capacity. Focus on safety, assistance, and needed recovery. Earnest preparation retains value without guaranteeing avoidance of every loss. Evaluate fairly without adding accusations increasing families' existing difficulty.

Dear friends, when helping neighbours, observe ability and safety directions. Do not create new risks to seem brave. Help can include accurate information, appropriate supplies, or support for responders. Many roles are useful. Cooperation helps accept personal limits while remaining present in responsibilities properly possible.

Let us seek an earnest outward self and a surrendered inward self. May Allah protect family and community, guide preparation, and strengthen those affected. May claims of surrender not stop effort, and demands to control every result not remove peace. May His help accompany every step for shared safety and goodness. Amin.
Wassalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh.

Consider who requires particular help and how to contact the right people. Do not spread panic-provoking assumptions. Prayers for protection accompany orderly effort. We need not wait for certainty of complete safety before responsibility. A clear preparation opportunity can be used while acknowledging much remains beyond human ability.

“If we prepare and still suffer loss, has effort failed?” Preparation guarantees no avoidance of every consequence, dear congregation. Its value remains as effort to fulfil a trust. If disaster occurs, focus on safety and needed help. Do not immediately blame victims or declare insufficient faith. Evaluate with enough information and fairness. This wisdom brings outward obedience and inward surrender together. Hands attend to what is possible; the heart does not demand power over every result. We learn from shortcomings without adding accusations making help harder to receive.

Dear congregation, let us imagine a short conversation. I ask, “Does the family know what steps to take when a local warning appears?” Then imagine someone here answering from everyday experience. We do not need to guess the most impressive answer. An honest answer helps this discussion more. If a part is difficult, name the difficulty without dismissing the wisdom's message. Then look for one step that is still possible. Conversation often becomes more useful when we stop trying to defeat one another and begin asking about real needs. In that way, advice can accompany us when facing a problem, instead of becoming an extra burden that merely sounds good in a gathering.
