Dear congregation, may Allah honour us, before the inspiration of this lesson passes, let us choose a practical exercise about combining safety preparation with tawakkul. We do not all have to choose the same step. Our families, work, and abilities differ. What matters is that our choice follows the wisdom's message and respects the obligations we already have. Allow a reasonable time to try it. If a change affects others, listen to their views. We are learning to develop habits we can practise in real life. Advice then begins to shape how we handle our responsibilities, instead of remaining something we agree with during the gathering.

Dear friends, take a moment to connect this explanation with a decision we once made. If we could go through that experience again, what would we want to improve? Of course, we cannot turn back time. But what we learned can still help us face the next situation. Keep one clear lesson. If someone's rights still need to be fulfilled, consider a proper way to fulfil them. Reflection becomes useful when it helps us move forward in the life we are living now.

If we can already begin, act without waiting for every circumstance to become perfect. We have an opportunity to make an effort today, and we continue asking Allah for help. phrasesEn: مَتَى جَعَلَكَ فِي الظَّاهِرِ مُمْتَثِلًا لِأَمْرِهِ
When He makes your outward self obedient to His command
وَرَزَقَكَ فِي الْبَاطِنِ الِاسْتِسْلَامَ لِقَهْرِهِ،
and grants your inward self surrender to His power,
فَقَدْ أَعْظَمَ الْمِنَّةَ عَلَيْكَ.
He has indeed bestowed a great favour upon you.

121.translation: Not everyone proven to have received special distinction has completed their inner purification.
syarahEn: People may have abilities, influence, or apparently special experiences yet retain shortcomings needing improvement. This wisdom warns against equating a particular gift with inner perfection. Devotion still needs knowledge, self-control, and openness to correction, however much trust people give.

Takhsis means granting special distinction. Takhlis refers to purification. Their similar sounds emphasize different meanings: receiving a special gift does not automatically mean every self-interest has been cleansed. Kamula means complete, restraining far-reaching conclusions about ourselves or someone admired.

A speaker may touch many hearts while still needing to learn good treatment of family. Someone skilled at organizing can still misuse power. Their benefits may be appreciated, but mistakes still require fair attention. Distinction does not make anyone immune to religious guidance or social responsibility.

For yourself, receive gifts as trusts needing care. Do not treat praise as proof that cleansing the heart is finished. Allow people to correct you and be willing to repair mistakes' effects. For others, combine appreciation with reasonable assessment of actions. This wisdom guards against idolization and pride. Ability can develop while purification continues, making gifts more beneficial rather than excuses to overlook visible wrongdoing.
shortEn: Assalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh. Alhamdulillah, all praise belongs to Allah. May blessings and peace be upon Prophet Muhammad, his family, and his Companions.

Dear congregation, we may greatly admire a teacher. Explanations touch us, knowledge is broad, and many feel helped. Admiration deserves healthy respect. Yet do not assume every action must be right. When problems arise, honesty, evidence, and fair handling remain necessary without erasing rights of those possibly harmed by particular behaviour.

Ibn 'Ata'illah reminds us that apparent distinction does not automatically mean complete inner purification. Takhsis concerns special distinction, while takhlis concerns purification. We appreciate gifts without treating anyone as immune to guidance. This also guards us when able or influential, so past benefits never justify rejecting every correction.

Dear friends, on hearing troubling news, do not immediately spread or deny it simply because you like the figure involved. Check through appropriate channels. Dear congregation, we may greatly admire a teacher. Explanations touch us, knowledge is broad, and many feel helped. Admiration deserves healthy respect. Yet do not assume every action must be right. When problems arise, honesty, evidence, and fair handling remain necessary without erasing rights of those possibly harmed by particular behaviour.

Dear congregation, may Allah have mercy on us, imagine taking this reminder home with us. We have taken off our shoes, the gathering is over, and ordinary life begins again. That is where the lesson about respecting teachers while maintaining justice will be tested. We may still face the same situation, the same people, and old habits that have not yet changed. We need to understand the message well enough to bring it into those circumstances. Listen slowly. If a sentence speaks to our situation, keep it in mind for later. We do not have to remember every explanation. One sound understanding, put sincerely into practice, is already worth working towards today.

People may have abilities, influence, or apparently special experiences yet retain shortcomings needing improvement. This wisdom warns against equating a particular gift with inner perfection. Devotion still needs knowledge, self-control, and openness to correction, however much trust people give.

Takhsis means granting special distinction. Takhlis refers to purification. Their similar sounds emphasize different meanings: receiving a special gift does not automatically mean every self-interest has been cleansed. Kamula means complete, restraining far-reaching conclusions about ourselves or someone admired.

Dear congregation, a saying of wisdom may be very short, yet reflection reveals how deeply it touches our long-standing habits. We are seeing that here in the matter of respecting teachers while maintaining justice. Its brevity should not make us feel that we have finished understanding it. Try expressing its meaning again in our own words. If it still seems unclear, return to the earlier example. We are not competing to memorize terminology. We want guidance we can use. In this way, a word that once sounded unfamiliar can help us recognize a mistaken step before the habit makes life harder for us or for others.
EXAMPLES AND CONVERSATION WITH THE CONGREGATION

Dear friends, on hearing troubling news, do not immediately spread or deny it simply because you like the figure involved. Check through appropriate channels. Someone sharing an experience should not be pressured merely to preserve a perfect image. We may appreciate knowledge and help while acknowledging harmful actions still need examination. Truth must not depend on how much we like the person discussed.

“If wrongdoing is found, must all their knowledge be discarded?” Assessment requires care, dear congregation. Practical benefits may be recognized and responsibility still remains. Do not use either to erase the other. This wisdom distinguishes special gifts from complete purification. Similar-sounding terms remind us distinction does not free humans from correction. For ourselves, do not feel safe from mistakes because many trust us. For someone admired, offer healthy respect and room for fair accountability.

Dear friends, if we sat in a circle after the lesson, someone might raise this question: “Does admiration make us reject information before proper examination?” That question deserves to be heard. We should not rush to answer before understanding the difficulty. We can begin by restating the issue in simple language, then consider the available choices. If we do not know the whole answer, we can admit it and continue learning. What matters is that the conversation leads towards a good action. Now think about the answer we would give a friend. Choose words that are clear and gentle, without promising an outcome beyond human ability.
PERSONAL REFLECTION

A speaker may touch many hearts while still needing to learn good treatment of family. Someone skilled at organizing can still misuse power. Their benefits may be appreciated, but mistakes still require fair attention. Distinction does not make anyone immune to religious guidance or social responsibility.

Explain boundaries, respect rights, and use outside help when issues require it. Influence is a trust monitored through actual behaviour. The greater the trust, the more important openness and responsibility towards those receiving guidance.

Dear congregation, try looking at our own journey with both honesty and compassion. In the matter of respecting teachers while maintaining justice, we may have made small progress for which we have never given thanks. There may also be a mistake we keep wanting to hide. Both can teach us without being put on display. Give thanks for the help that has already come, then examine what needs improving. Do not compare our whole journey with a fragment of someone else's life. We have real responsibilities today. Recognizing our part allows reflection to move into action, so regret need not remain a thought circling endlessly without direction.

Dear friends, take a moment to connect this explanation with a decision we once made. If we could go through that experience again, what would we want to improve? Of course, we cannot turn back time. But what we learned can still help us face the next situation. Keep one clear lesson. If someone's rights still need to be fulfilled, consider a proper way to fulfil them. Reflection becomes useful when it helps us move forward in the life we are living now.
PRACTICAL STEPS TO TRY

For yourself, receive gifts as trusts needing care. Do not treat praise as proof that cleansing the heart is finished. Allow people to correct you and be willing to repair mistakes' effects. For others, combine appreciation with reasonable assessment of actions. This wisdom guards against idolization and pride. Ability can develop while purification continues, making gifts more beneficial rather than excuses to overlook visible wrongdoing.

For practice, examine responses to reports about a liked figure. Restrain sharing and seek information through appropriate people. If asked to hear someone's experience, do not immediately require public proof before a crowd. Direct towards competent support according to need. Maintain manners when asking and raising concerns. May respect for teachers nurture love of knowledge and truth rather than unlimited defence neglecting affected people's dignity or rights.

Now let us turn the lesson about respecting teachers while maintaining justice into a simple plan, dear friends. Choose one action with a reasonably clear time for doing it. Do not immediately promise to change our whole life. Ask when we can begin and what needs preparing. If other people are involved, speak with them properly; do not make decisions on their behalf in a passing burst of enthusiasm. After trying, notice what helped and what still got in the way. We may adjust our approach while keeping the right aim. A small exercise gives us a chance to learn from real circumstances, so a good intention takes a form we can actually carry out.

Dear congregation, if we wish to respond, sharing the general lesson is enough. We do not need to name anyone or reveal anybody's private affairs. Listen calmly to different responses. There may be circumstances we have never considered. After listening, return to the message we are studying and consider the most appropriate action. Learning together can broaden our understanding, provided the conversation respects people's dignity and does not become a place for judging their experiences.

Dear congregation, after hearing this explanation about respecting teachers while maintaining justice, keep one insight that is closest to our circumstances. We can recall it on the journey home or discuss it with our family without talking down to them. Ask ourselves which part we have understood and which part needs further study. In this way, the conversation continues naturally beyond the gathering. We do not need to monitor other people's inner states. It is enough to care for the responsibilities already before us. May this little knowledge help us choose a step pleasing to Allah when we face the matter in real life.

Let us seek love of knowledge accompanied by clarity. May Allah bless trustworthy teachers, protect vulnerable people, and guide fair resolution. May admiration not close courage to face reality. Not everyone proven to have received distinction
كَمُلَ تَخْلِيصُهُ.
has completed their inner purification.

122.translation: Only someone deeply ignorant belittles a wird. Spiritual gifts may still be encountered in the Hereafter, but the opportunity to perform a wird ends with worldly life. What deserves greater attention is the opportunity that cannot be replaced once gone. A wird is what He asks of you, while a spiritual gift is what you ask of Him. Can what He asks of you be compared with what you ask of Him?
syarahEn: We can be more interested in awaiting calm, deep understanding, or inner experience than maintaining simple practices. Ibn 'Ata'illah warns against belittling a wird. While alive, we can fulfil required devotion. That opportunity will end, while Allah's giving exceeds experiences sought now.

Al-wird is regular practice following guidance. Al-warid is a gift coming to the heart. Yantawi means ending or being folded away, while la yukhlafu wujuduh refers to an opportunity irreplaceable once gone. The distinction orders priorities: practice is responsibility performed, while gifts are giving requested.

Someone may not yet feel hoped-for attentiveness, but can still maintain recitation and obligations orderly. That perseverance need not be left because inner experience has not arrived. Conversely, someone receiving peace still maintains deeds without treating the feeling as completed learning. We protect continuity in devotion within ability.

Arrange a realistic wird whose basis you understand. Prioritize obligations, health, and family rights, seeking guidance before adding particular practices. If interrupted, return orderly without creating unsustainable burdens. This wisdom teaches appreciation of time. Do not waste available opportunity awaiting gifts beyond our control. Fulfil today's devotion honestly, then seek bounty and acceptance from Allah, who knows every servant's needs.
shortEn: Assalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh. Alhamdulillah, all praise belongs to Allah. May blessings and peace be upon Prophet Muhammad, his family, and his Companions.

Dear friends, may Allah have mercy on us, some await a special feeling to become enthusiastic about worship. They want strong peace or an experience making life different. Without it, routine practice seems ordinary. Yet passing days reduce opportunities for goodness. What we await may not arrive as desired, while today's obligations clearly need a place.

Ibn 'Ata'illah distinguishes wird and warid. A wird is regular practice following guidance, while a warid is a gift coming to the heart. Worldly opportunities for deeds will end, but Allah's generosity exceeds present experiences. He invites maintaining required devotion rather than spending attention awaiting gifts whose form and timing exceed our control.

Dear congregation, choose practices understood and suited to circumstances. Prioritize obligations and family rights. Seek sound guidance before adding particular practices. We need not force large amounts to feel earnest. Realistic routines support perseverance, allowing worship without continual neglect of bodily needs or other obligatory responsibilities.

“What if it feels flat?” Keep learning meanings and improving attention. Peace does not always arrive with intense atmosphere. We may appreciate fulfilling duties without special experiences. If interrupted, return orderly. Do not make one failure a reason to leave every good habit, or continually add punishment burdens that cannot be maintained.

Dear friends, today's opportunity matters because it cannot be recalled once gone. One maintained obligation and one fulfilled right are practical work. We need not await major events to acknowledge their benefit. Those sharing life can feel perseverance through better guarded words and responsibilities beyond stories of worship experiences.

Let us value practices possible now. May Allah grant perseverance, accept little good, and protect against chasing experiences until duties are forgotten. May life be used honestly and with balance. When requesting gifts, may we also receive ability to fulfil devotion already clearly within today's reach and responsibility. Amin.
Wassalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh.

Seek proper guidance before adding particular practices, protecting body and family rights. Realistic routines give perseverance room. Perhaps an answer comes straight away; perhaps a difficulty comes to mind instead. Let us hear that difficulty calmly. Good advice needs to meet the reality of life, including the limitations we face. Now imagine someone we love asking that question. Would our answer help them act, or simply leave them feeling scolded? Here we learn to convey the truth in a way that can be received. We also need honesty that gives direction when speaking to ourselves, so that understanding a problem gives us courage to begin putting it right.

We can examine all of this calmly. Turn our attention towards an action we can manage today, then ask Allah for help with the next stage of the process.

Ask a suitable teacher about anything unclear. Families can remind politely while protecting shared rights. May today's opportunity be used earnestly and perseverance grow through orderly devotion even without extraordinary experiences once imagined.

Dear congregation, if we want to take one task home from this discussion of maintaining regular practice without awaiting special experiences, choose something we can truly do. There is no need to announce it now. We can decide after getting home, when we have a fuller picture of our circumstances. Make the step small enough for us to know when it will be done. If there are obstacles, consider what reasonable help we need. We may also ask a trusted person to remind us respectfully. Change requires our involvement, as well as a heart that feels inspired. Let us accompany a good intention with preparation that makes it easier to carry out.

Dear friends, we can pause before answering a question that feels close to home. Sometimes our first answer comes from a habit of defending ourselves. Given time, we can hear the advice more clearly. We do not have to make everyone speak immediately. Some people think more easily in silence, while others are helped by asking questions. What matters is making room to understand, then choosing a step sincerely. We want to learn in a way that preserves good manners and makes our responsibilities clearer.

Dear congregation, may Allah have mercy on us, choose one sentence from our discussion of maintaining regular practice without awaiting special experiences that we want to remember tomorrow. Repeat its meaning silently in our own words. We do not need the sentence that sounds most impressive. Choose what helps most when facing real circumstances. Then ask Allah to enable us to put it into practice. We also pray for those struggling in similar circumstances. phrasesEn: لَا يَسْتَحْقِرُ الْوِرْدَ إِلَّا جَهُولٌ.
Only someone deeply ignorant belittles a wird.
الْوَارِدُ يُوجَدُ فِي الدَّارِ الْآخِرَةِ،
Spiritual gifts may still be encountered in the Hereafter.
الْوِرْدُ يَنْطَوِي بِانْطِوَاءِ هَذِهِ الدَّارِ،
The opportunity to perform a wird ends with worldly life.
وَأَوْلَى مَا يُعْتَنَى بِهِ مَا لَا يُخْلَفُ وُجُودُهُ.
What deserves greater attention is the opportunity that cannot be replaced once gone.
الْوِرْدُ هُوَ طَالِبُهُ مِنْكَ
A wird is what He asks of you,
وَالْوَارِدُ أَنْتَ تَطْلُبُهُ مِنْهُ،
while a spiritual gift is what you ask of Him.
وَأَيْنَ مَا هُوَ طَالِبُهُ مِنْكَ مِمَّا هُوَ مَطْلَبُكَ مِنْهُ؟
Can what He asks of you be compared with what you ask of Him?

123.translation: Spiritual help arrives according to the recipient's readiness. Lights rise according to the clarity of their inner secrets.
syarahEn: A heart continually filled with hatred and self-defence struggles to accept advice even when the lesson is clear. Conversely, a heart willing to be cleansed has more room to understand. This wisdom invites inner preparation so arriving help is not obstructed by habits we can actually improve.

Al-isti'dad means readiness to receive. Safa' al-asrar means clarity of inner depths. Wurud al-imdad refers to arriving help, while shuruq al-anwar portrays the rising light of knowledge. We may read the metaphor like preparing a vessel: its cleanliness and capacity affect received benefit. Readiness remains the servant's work, while gifts do not become Allah's debt to them.

This therefore accords with Wisdom 79 about gifts arriving unexpectedly. We prepare through repentance, learning, and honesty without assuming preparation gives power to determine when a particular experience arrives. If advice remains unclear, examine what is still rejected through pride or self-interest.

Practice can begin with listening fully and admitting one mistake without immediate excuses. Reduce speech damaging the heart and fulfil delayed rights. These simple efforts help clarity grow. Do not measure readiness only through comfort or mastery of spiritual language. This wisdom returns us to practical work: cleansing receptivity so guidance more readily bears action. Afterwards, we remain grateful, seek help, and receive gifts as Allah's generosity.
shortEn: Assalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh. Alhamdulillah, all praise belongs to Allah. May blessings and peace be upon Prophet Muhammad, his family, and his Companions.

Dear congregation, someone can attend learning with an open book but locked heart. Every explanation immediately meets comparison with personal opinion. If different, the mind prepares rebuttals before understanding. We want benefit but give no room for unknown information to enter and be calmly examined. Learning tires because all attention maintains the appearance of being right.

Ibn 'Ata'illah recalls the relationship between readiness and arriving help, and inner clarity and rising knowledge's light. We prepare without treating preparation as a guarantee binding Allah. A more spacious heart receives lessons more readily. Yet we still learn through sound knowledge and careful judgement rather than swallowing every statement to appear open to advice.

State differences politely. Critical thought can accompany humility, because respecting knowledge does not require pretending to understand confusing matters.

The lesson is not allowing one experience to close every path towards good. Seek suitable support if wounds make learning or daily relationships persistently difficult.

Dear congregation, readiness also appears after learning. Choose one practice and allow evaluation time. No need to transform the whole life overnight. Notice obstructive habits and reduce gradually. We clear room for growing benefit while seeking Allah's help because understanding and doing good rest beyond personal will alone.

Let us arrive as people still able to learn. May Allah clear hearts, bring sound knowledge, and help us accept correction with dignity. May readiness bring practical benefit rather than pride in being most open. May understanding gain a place in actions and make us gentler towards fellow learners. Amin.
Wassalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh.

Dear friends, we can pause before answering a question that feels close to home. Sometimes our first answer comes from a habit of defending ourselves. Given time, we can hear the advice more clearly. What matters is making room to understand, then choosing a step sincerely. We want to learn in a way that preserves good manners and makes our responsibilities clearer.
PRACTICAL STEPS TO TRY

Practice can begin with listening fully and admitting one mistake without immediate excuses. Reduce speech damaging the heart and fulfil delayed rights. These simple efforts help clarity grow. Do not measure readiness only through comfort or mastery of spiritual language. This wisdom returns us to practical work: cleansing receptivity so guidance more readily bears action. Afterwards, we remain grateful, seek help, and receive gifts as Allah's generosity.

For practice, identify one thing to understand before a study session. Listen to a sufficiently complete explanation and ask unclear points politely. If disagreeing, give reasons without contempt. Afterwards, choose one understanding to apply. Teachers also need room for questions and correction. May readiness grow both ways, helping knowledge benefit. We want spacious hearts and honest minds so learning is not entirely spent maintaining an image of already being right.

Dear friends, test our plan against everyday situations. When we face the matter of preparing to listen before composing a rebuttal again, what will change in our actions? Choose an answer we can recognize, such as having a conversation or stopping a habit. If the answer is still too general, make the step smaller. We are not writing a beautiful promise for others. We are preparing help for ourselves when we encounter an old habit. After doing it, give thanks and keep learning. If it has not worked yet, examine the reason honestly, then try again with preparation better suited to the situation.

Let us leave room for questions that remain unresolved, dear congregation. If confusion remains after the gathering, write down the issue clearly. Then ask someone who understands the subject and knows the circumstances involved. We may learn gradually. A little accurate understanding is more helpful than a rushed decision made simply because we want to feel that everything is settled. Meanwhile, continue fulfilling our clear obligations and respect the rights of those around us.
REINFORCING THE MESSAGE AND CLOSING SUPPLICATION

Let us recall the direction of today's discussion, dear congregation. The lesson about preparing to listen before composing a rebuttal invites us to examine our own choices and improve what is our responsibility. After returning home, things may feel ordinary again. That is where a good intention needs attention. We can remind ourselves gently while remaining firm about our obligations. If we need to begin again one day, let us begin. The opportunity to learn is not exhausted because one attempt has not gone smoothly. While we have the ability and opportunity, let us keep seeking goodness and asking Allah to guide our hearts and accept our deeds.

Let us arrive as people still able to learn. May Allah clear hearts, bring sound knowledge, and help us accept correction with dignity. May readiness bring practical benefit rather than pride in being most open. May understanding gain a place in actions and make us gentler towards fellow learners. Amin.
Wassalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh.
phrasesEn: وُرُودُ الْإِمْدَادِ بِحَسَبِ الِاسْتِعْدَادِ،
Spiritual help arrives according to the recipient's readiness.
وَشُرُوقُ الْأَنْوَارِ عَلَى حَسَبِ صَفَاءِ الْأَسْرَارِ.
Light rises according to the clarity of their inner secrets.

124.translation: On entering the morning, the heedless person thinks only of what they will do. The person of understanding attends to what Allah does with them.
syarahEn: Every morning we may plan and identify necessary work. What needs care is assuming the entire day runs through personal will. This wisdom distinguishes heedless attention from understanding: the first fixates on personal action, while the second also recognizes Allah's sustaining care.

Al-ghafil means the heedless person. Al-'aqil is someone using understanding clearly. The difference between yaf'alu, what they do, and yaf'alu Allahu bihi, what Allah does with them, shifts attention's centre. Human plans are placed within the reality that health, opportunities, and results are not entirely under personal power.

For example, a teacher prepares a good schedule then finds a student needs another approach. Someone fixed solely on plans may become angry that circumstances disobey. Someone more aware still arranges lessons while reading actual needs. Change is accepted as part of the trust requiring response rather than merely an interruption to personal will.

Begin with clear aims, supplication for help, and readiness to adjust when circumstances change. Planning still proceeds responsibly. What loosens is the demand to control everything. At night, evaluate efforts while remembering help received. This wisdom helps greater presence in life, with attention beyond task lists to how Allah teaches through success, limitations, and responsibilities arriving throughout the day.
shortEn: Assalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh. Alhamdulillah, all praise belongs to Allah. May blessings and peace be upon Prophet Muhammad, his family, and his Companions.

Dear friends, may Allah honour us, morning can begin with neat plans: this work by one time, the next task afterwards. Suddenly a child has fever or a neighbour urgently needs help. Irritation comes because the agenda is ruined. We feel the day failed before seeing a new duty requiring consideration alongside existing responsibilities.

Ibn 'Ata'illah distinguishes heedless attention from understanding. One thinks only of personal actions, while another also notices what Allah brings into life. We still plan, but with awareness that health, opportunities, and human needs can change. Wisdom is therefore needed to respond when reality does not follow last night's arrangements.

Dear congregation, in urgency assess need and safety first. Help according to ability and responsibility. Then inform those waiting for your work. Honesty about change is better than disappearing and making impossible promises. We rearrange steps so attention to new needs does not immediately leave other rights forgotten without explanation.

“If everyone asks for help, when will my duties finish?” Reasonable boundaries are needed. Every request need not be handled personally. Ask urgency and direct to a more suitable person when needed. Reading today's trusts requires clarity, including when to help directly and when to preserve work that cannot be left because others depend on its result.

Dear friends, believers need not interpret every change as a definite special message. Simply respond through knowledge, character, and sound judgement. Help sincerely when possible; express limits politely. We seek guidance while admitting the entire day exceeds personal control despite careful preparation.

Let us open morning with plans and prayer for ability to meet what arrives. May Allah grant family health, ease work, and guide priorities when schedules change. May disappointment not fall on those needing help. May earnest work accompany spacious hearts, so a day different from plans still contains practical responsibility and good. Amin.
Wassalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh.

Those who are older can still discover a new understanding, and children can still bring serious questions. Let us listen with an open heart. Morning plans are neat when news arrives that a relative needs assistance. We immediately consider the day failed. Dear friends, before that judgement, examine present circumstances. Assess need and safety and help responsibly. If other work must change, inform those waiting rather than leaving guesses. Plans guide, but must meet reality. We can rearrange without considering every preparation useless. Honest information helps many rights remain considered when a new need takes priority.

“If requests keep coming, when can I manage my duties?” We need boundaries, dear congregation. The same person need not give every assistance. Ask urgency and whether someone else is more suitable. Refusal with proper explanation may preserve an unleaveable trust. This wisdom shifts attention from controlling the agenda towards awareness of Allah's arrangements. It neither removes planning nor commands accepting every request. We still judge clearly, use ability, and acknowledge health and opportunities do not entirely follow personal schedules.

Now try answering silently, dear friends: “How can we help an urgent situation without disappearing from other responsibilities?” There is no need to hurry. People may give different answers because their circumstances also differ. We listen while holding to the guidance that is already clear. If someone is new to learning, give them a chance to ask. If someone has made a mistake, do not make their experience a joke. A safe conversation gives us courage to examine our own habits. Then we can choose a reasonable improvement. May a gathering like this send us home with the courage to learn, rather than merely the ability to comment on other people's lives.

Dear friends, before moving to practical steps, let us give ourselves room to absorb this. The lesson about rearranging plans when new needs arise may touch an experience that is still unresolved. We do not have to force all our feelings into order tonight. Simply recognize one part that now seems clearer. Perhaps we need to apologize, seek an explanation, or change how we make decisions. Perhaps we first need rest so that we can think clearly. We can examine all of this calmly. Turn our attention towards an action we can manage today, then ask Allah for help with the next stage of the process.

Then ask someone who understands the subject and knows the circumstances involved. We may learn gradually. For practice, choose one habit of providing updates when plans change. Prepare honest words about need and ability without overpromising every task by its old time. If helping, make your part clear. Direct to others respectfully if needed. Family can discuss sharing so requests do not always accumulate on one person. May schedules support order and openness reveal arriving duties, allowing change to receive responsibility and good manners.

Let us arrange a step that fits our lives, dear congregation. The lesson about rearranging plans when new needs arise will be easier to remember when connected with a time or activity that already exists. We do not need to add burdens without considering our ability. Choose a reasonable place to begin, and respect other people's rights as we act. Children may ask for their parents' support; adults can also seek advice when struggling. We do not have to face everything alone. What we want to nurture is a willingness to do our part properly and in an orderly way, even when the results still take time to appear.

Dear congregation, try practising that answer in our own words. Imagine a family member asking while we are relaxing. We do not need to give a long sermon. Begin by listening, then share what we truly understand. If something remains unclear, say that we will learn more. A simple conversation like this helps us check our own understanding while ensuring that advice is given respectfully. We learn together, without needing to appear as people who have already resolved every problem.
REINFORCING THE MESSAGE AND CLOSING SUPPLICATION

Dear congregation, after hearing this explanation about rearranging plans when new needs arise, keep one insight that is closest to our circumstances. We can recall it on the journey home or discuss it with our family without talking down to them. Ask ourselves which part we have understood and which part needs further study. In this way, the conversation continues naturally beyond the gathering. We do not need to monitor other people's inner states. It is enough to care for the responsibilities already before us. May this little knowledge help us choose a step pleasing to Allah when we face the matter in real life.

Let us open morning with plans and prayer for ability to meet what arrives. May Allah grant family health, ease work, and guide priorities when schedules change. phrasesEn: الْغَافِلُ إِذَا أَصْبَحَ نَظَرَ فِيمَا يَفْعَلُ،
On entering the morning, the heedless person thinks only of what they will do.
وَالْعَاقِلُ يَنْظُرُ مَاذَا يَفْعَلُ اللَّهُ بِهِ.
The person of understanding attends to what Allah does with them.

125.translation: Worshippers and ascetics feel unsettled by things because their hearts have not witnessed Allah through them. If they witnessed Him through all things, nothing would unsettle them.
syarahEn: Some withdraw from many things for fear of attachment to the world. Caution can help, but can also make life feel full of threats. This wisdom invites devotion to grow until encounters with creation increasingly recall Allah rather than continually leaving the heart directionless.

Al-'ubbad means devoted worshippers, while al-zuhhad means those practising detachment from the world. Istawhasha describes estrangement or unease. Shuhuduhu refers to the heart witnessing signs of Allah's power. Witnessing through all things means awareness of the Creator through creation, without imagining Allah within objects.

For example, work can be seen solely as busyness interrupting worship. With broader understanding, lawful work becomes a place for honesty and benefit. Family care can also be practical devotion. The heart learns not to separate the whole of life from relationship with Allah, provided means and aims remain guided.

We still need to avoid clearly harmful things and recognize personal capacity. Human unease has many causes, so it should not judge someone's faith as low. Use this wisdom to broaden attention. Ask what good is possible now. With knowledge's guidance, creation becomes a place to read signs and fulfil trusts. The heart can be calmer among people because devotion is sought through responsibility and compassion as well as distance.
shortEn: Assalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh. Alhamdulillah, all praise belongs to Allah. May blessings and peace be upon Prophet Muhammad, his family, and his Companions.

Dear congregation, some find it difficult to guard the heart in busy places. Markets have many offers, work many competitions, and journeys many attractions. They hope to withdraw from everything for lasting calm. A pause can help, but life still brings human encounters and needs we cannot entirely leave.

Ibn 'Ata'illah reminds us that unease before creation relates to attention not yet directed towards Allah through His signs. We do not understand Allah as dwelling within objects. We train awareness of the Creator when meeting creation. Life's encounters can recall obedience, so busyness need not always seem an interruption cutting off every path of devotion.

Dear friends, while shopping we can bargain respectfully and honour sellers' work. While selling, describe goods accurately. While walking, protect others' rights to shared space. These simple choices connect faith and action. We need not await silence to remember Allah knows how we use opportunities and treat those encountered.

“What if the atmosphere really makes temptation easier?” Recognize limits and arrange involvement. Bring a needs list, reduce unnecessary exposure, and choose suitable times. We may still leave clearly harmful circumstances. This wisdom broadens life's view rather than asking us to ignore known capacities and risks. Awareness and adjustment can protect the heart together.

Dear congregation, lawful work can gain devotion's direction when rights and obligations are protected. This does not make every activity automatically good through good intention alone. Methods still need examination. We learn daily opportunities for obedience while seeking help so crowds do not make us forget and pleasure does not permit neglect of guidance and trusts.

Let us bring remembrance of Allah into ordinary encounters. May He protect hearts in crowds, guide transactions and work, and help respect people. May creation remind us of Him so daily life feels connected to devotion. May we return from busyness with protected trusts and benefit others can feel. Amin.
Wassalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh.

Then look for one step that is still possible. Conversation often becomes more useful when we stop trying to defeat one another and begin asking about real needs. Dear congregation, try looking at our own journey with both honesty and compassion. In the matter of remembering Allah through choices amid a busy market, we may have made small progress for which we have never given thanks. There may also be a mistake we keep wanting to hide. Dear congregation, may Allah honour us, before the inspiration of this lesson passes, let us choose a practical exercise about remembering Allah through choices amid a busy market. Advice then begins to shape how we handle our responsibilities, instead of remaining something we agree with during the gathering.

Dear friends, before we close, silently recall the lesson we most want to take home. Today we have spoken about remembering Allah through choices amid a busy market. phrasesEn: إِنَّمَا اسْتَوْحَشَ الْعُبَّادُ وَالزُّهَّادُ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ
Worshippers and ascetics feel unsettled by all things
لِغَيْبَتِهِمْ عَنِ اللَّهِ فِي كُلِّ شَيْءٍ،
because their hearts have not witnessed Allah through them.
فَلَوْ شَهِدُوهُ فِي كُلِّ شَيْءٍ
If they witnessed Him through all things,
لَمْ يَسْتَوْحِشُوا مِنْ شَيْءٍ.
nothing would unsettle them.

126.translation: In this worldly abode He commands you to reflect on His creations. In the abode of the Hereafter He will unveil to you the perfection of His Essence.
syarahEn: In this world, people know guidance about Allah through revelation and reflection on creation. We see order, change, and creatures' dependence, acknowledging the Creator's greatness. This wisdom places that worldly task within hope for the Hereafter's gift, giving our search direction while recognizing human knowledge's limits.

Al-nazar means attentive looking or reflection. Mukawwanatihi refers to His creations. Tilka al-dar directs attention to the Hereafter, while kamal dhatih refers to the perfection of Allah's Essence. This hope is understood within Sunni belief in believers being granted the vision of Allah, without imagining form, direction, or a manner resembling seeing created beings.

Our present task is responding to guidance with faith and devotion. Reflecting on the body, care for health as a trust. Observing society, practise justice and compassion. Knowledge of creation can serve gratitude provided it does not nurture the assumption that reason can fully encompass Allah's reality.

Do not force an experience of seeing Allah's Essence as a goal for worldly practice. Accept limits directing us towards commanded work. Learning, worship, and others' rights are clear paths. Hope for the Hereafter gives longing and steadfastness, while worldly reflection supplies daily devotion. This wisdom helps us walk with knowledge sufficient for obedience and humility to acknowledge Allah's majesty beyond human images and measures.
shortEn: Assalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh. Alhamdulillah, all praise belongs to Allah. May blessings and peace be upon Prophet Muhammad, his family, and his Companions.

Dear friends, may Allah have mercy on us, looking at the night sky can briefly pause busyness. Its expanse is greater than our garden and the problems filling our minds. We are not asked to forget problems but given an opportunity to locate ourselves humbly. Human life has limits, while much beyond remains unknown and uncontrollable.

Ibn 'Ata'illah reminds us that here we are commanded to reflect on Allah's creation, while the Hereafter brings a different gift. Sunni belief includes believers being granted the vision of Allah without imagining form, direction, or a manner resembling sight of creatures. We do not portray His Essence through objects. Today's task is receiving guidance and serving with knowledge and humility.

Dear congregation, reflection can begin nearby: which blessings are being used and which trusts remain neglected? The vast sky recalls knowledge's limits without erasing duties at home. Afterwards, perhaps someone needs contacting or work completing. We want wonder to improve order in life beyond a feeling of smallness soon forgotten.

“How does studying nature relate to faith?” Knowledge can help recognize order and care responsibly for creation. Learn from sound sources and maintain humility about understanding's limits. Do not rush into baseless claims. Wonder at creation should increase gratitude and care in speech, especially about Allah and matters beyond our reach.

Dear friends, hope for the Hereafter also helps us consider deeds we will carry. Time remains for forgiveness and restored rights. We need not await extraordinary experiences to fulfil that task. Learning, honest work, and family care remain clear paths. Good reflection returns to devotion possible in present circumstances.

Let us seek knowledge making hearts submissive. May Allah guide reflection, protect faith from mistaken images, and grant strengthening hope for the Hereafter. May creation's vastness bring humility without worthlessness. May entrusted time serve proper responsibilities and practical compassion towards others. Amin.
Wassalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh.

If a sentence speaks to our situation, keep it in mind for later. We do not have to remember every explanation. One sound understanding, put sincerely into practice, is already worth working towards today.
CORE WISDOM

Ibn 'Ata'illah reminds us that here we are commanded to reflect on Allah's creation, while the Hereafter brings a different gift. Sunni belief includes believers being granted the vision of Allah without imagining form, direction, or a manner resembling sight of creatures. We do not portray His Essence through objects. Today's task is receiving guidance and serving with knowledge and humility.

In this world, people know guidance about Allah through revelation and reflection on creation. We see order, change, and creatures' dependence, acknowledging the Creator's greatness. This wisdom places that worldly task within hope for the Hereafter's gift, giving our search direction while recognizing human knowledge's limits.

Al-nazar means attentive looking or reflection. Mukawwanatihi refers to His creations. Tilka al-dar directs attention to the Hereafter, while kamal dhatih refers to the perfection of Allah's Essence. This hope is understood within Sunni belief in believers being granted the vision of Allah, without imagining form, direction, or a manner resembling seeing created beings.

Dear friends, after hearing that explanation, give our minds room to connect its meaning with actual events. We need not use the lesson about reflecting on the sky humbly and remembering the Hereafter as a label for judging people's inner states. We see only part of their lives. For ourselves, this advice can become an honest question. What am I hoping for? What am I neglecting? Our answer may not be complete today. That is all right. What matters is being willing to learn sincerely, examine our understanding, and follow sound guidance when seeking to change our daily habits.
EXAMPLES AND CONVERSATION WITH THE CONGREGATION

Dear congregation, reflection can begin nearby: which blessings are being used and which trusts remain neglected? The vast sky recalls knowledge's limits without erasing duties at home. Afterwards, perhaps someone needs contacting or work completing. We want wonder to improve order in life beyond a feeling of smallness soon forgotten.

“How does studying nature relate to faith?” Knowledge can help recognize order and care responsibly for creation. Learn from sound sources and maintain humility about understanding's limits. Do not rush into baseless claims. Wonder at creation should increase gratitude and care in speech, especially about Allah and matters beyond our reach.

Night offers a chance to view the sky safely. Problems filling the mind remain, but we begin acknowledging limited vision. Dear friends, wonder can accompany nearby questions: which blessings remain in use and which trusts uncared for? We need not know the whole universe to give thanks. Sound knowledge can be learned gradually. Do not add baseless claims merely to make reflection sound impressive. Afterwards, home still needs presence. Words need care and tasks may be completed. Wonder benefits when it makes us more orderly and humble.

“How can we discuss the Hereafter's gift without portraying Allah like creatures?” Hold to properly taught understanding, dear congregation. In Sunni belief, believers hope for the vision of Allah in the Hereafter without imagining form, direction, or a manner resembling seeing creatures. We invent no details from imagination. This wisdom directs present reflection to creation and hope towards Allah's future generosity. Ask a knowledgeable teacher about unclear points. Knowledge's limits encourage caution, filling faith conversations with respect and willingness to learn.

Dear friends, if we sat in a circle after the lesson, someone might raise this question: “What can we bring home after marvelling at the sky's vastness?” That question deserves to be heard. We should not rush to answer before understanding the difficulty. We can begin by restating the issue in simple language, then consider the available choices. If we do not know the whole answer, we can admit it and continue learning. What matters is that the conversation leads towards a good action. Now think about the answer we would give a friend. Choose words that are clear and gentle, without promising an outcome beyond human ability.
PERSONAL REFLECTION

Our present task is responding to guidance with faith and devotion. Reflecting on the body, care for health as a trust. Observing society, practise justice and compassion. Knowledge of creation can serve gratitude provided it does not nurture the assumption that reason can fully encompass Allah's reality.

Dear friends, hope for the Hereafter also helps us consider deeds we will carry. Time remains for forgiveness and restored rights. We need not await extraordinary experiences to fulfil that task. Learning, honest work, and family care remain clear paths. Good reflection returns to devotion possible in present circumstances.

Dear friends, before moving to practical steps, let us give ourselves room to absorb this. The lesson about reflecting on the sky humbly and remembering the Hereafter may touch an experience that is still unresolved. We do not have to force all our feelings into order tonight. Simply recognize one part that now seems clearer. Perhaps we need to apologize, seek an explanation, or change how we make decisions. Perhaps we first need rest so that we can think clearly. We can examine all of this calmly. Turn our attention towards an action we can manage today, then ask Allah for help with the next stage of the process.

Dear friends, take a moment to connect this explanation with a decision we once made. If we could go through that experience again, what would we want to improve? Of course, we cannot turn back time. But what we learned can still help us face the next situation. Keep one clear lesson. If someone's rights still need to be fulfilled, consider a proper way to fulfil them. Reflection becomes useful when it helps us move forward in the life we are living now.
PRACTICAL STEPS TO TRY

Do not force an experience of seeing Allah's Essence as a goal for worldly practice. Accept limits directing us towards commanded work. Learning, worship, and others' rights are clear paths. Hope for the Hereafter gives longing and steadfastness, while worldly reflection supplies daily devotion. This wisdom helps us walk with knowledge sufficient for obedience and humility to acknowledge Allah's majesty beyond human images and measures.

For practice, briefly observe creation in a safe place. Choose one source of gratitude and connect it with responsible action. When studying nature, use reliable sources and distinguish knowledge from assumptions. Do not force every finding into a baseless religious claim. May reflection broaden attention, recall return to Allah, and increase care in speech. We return with wonder nurturing deeds and humility.

Now let us turn the lesson about reflecting on the sky humbly and remembering the Hereafter into a simple plan, dear friends. Choose one action with a reasonably clear time for doing it. Do not immediately promise to change our whole life. Ask when we can begin and what needs preparing. If other people are involved, speak with them properly; do not make decisions on their behalf in a passing burst of enthusiasm. After trying, notice what helped and what still got in the way. We may adjust our approach while keeping the right aim. A small exercise gives us a chance to learn from real circumstances, so a good intention takes a form we can actually carry out.

Dear congregation, if we wish to respond, sharing the general lesson is enough. We do not need to name anyone or reveal anybody's private affairs. Listen calmly to different responses. There may be circumstances we have never considered. After listening, return to the message we are studying and consider the most appropriate action. Learning together can broaden our understanding, provided the conversation respects people's dignity and does not become a place for judging their experiences.
REINFORCING THE MESSAGE AND CLOSING SUPPLICATION

Let us recall the direction of today's discussion, dear congregation. The lesson about reflecting on the sky humbly and remembering the Hereafter invites us to examine our own choices and improve what is our responsibility. After returning home, things may feel ordinary again. That is where a good intention needs attention. We can remind ourselves gently while remaining firm about our obligations. If we need to begin again one day, let us begin. The opportunity to learn is not exhausted because one attempt has not gone smoothly. While we have the ability and opportunity, let us keep seeking goodness and asking Allah to guide our hearts and accept our deeds.

Let us seek knowledge making hearts submissive. May Allah guide reflection, protect faith from mistaken images, and grant strengthening hope for the Hereafter. May creation's vastness bring humility without worthlessness. May entrusted time serve proper responsibilities and practical compassion towards others. Amin.
Wassalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh.

In this worldly abode He commands you to reflect on His creations.
وَسَيَكْشِفُ لَكَ فِي تِلْكَ الدَّارِ عَنْ كَمَالِ ذَاتِهِ.
In the Hereafter He will unveil to you the perfection of His Essence.

127.translation: He knows you cannot patiently bear distance from Him. Therefore He shows you the creations brought into existence by His will.
syarahEn: Longing for Allah can make the heart continually seek ways to remember Him. Yet humans live amid creation and have limits in knowing their Lord. This closing wisdom reveals Allah's generosity: visible life provides signs helping the heart remain connected through reflection, gratitude, and devotion.

'Alima minka means He knows about you. La tasbiru 'anhu describes profound need and longing for Him. Ashhadaka means He shows you, while ma baraza minhu refers to creation brought into existence through His will. Read this as guidance through creation's results rather than creatures being part of Allah's Essence.

We can remember His care through available food, human assistance, or bodily abilities continually working. Difficulty too reminds us of dependence. All provide reflection answered through actions: gratitude, help, forgiveness sought, and trusts protected. Knowing Allah need not await extraordinary events.

Closing the journey of 127 wisdoms, this lesson returns us to daily life. After understanding many terms, examine whether family, work, and social relationships improve. Use knowledge to order responses to life actually lived. A heart remembering Allah through creation need not withdraw from every responsibility. Responsibility itself becomes continually open devotion. We walk with longing nurtured by knowledge and compassion expressed through simple work possible honestly today.

Let us go home with one earnest step. May Allah accept learning time, protect intentions, and help bring benefit to family and neighbours. May encountered creation recall its Creator. May hearts remain near Him amid busyness, and may compassion discussed here truly reach those awaiting us at home. Amin.
Wassalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh.

We recognize help and opportunity through creation, directing gratitude to the Creator. That knowledge gives reasons to respect people and protect trusts rather than ignore life because spiritual learning supposedly exists only in thought.

Let me ask a question, dear congregation: “What small habit will help the lesson remain after the gathering ends?” Take a moment to think about it. Perhaps an answer comes straight away; perhaps a difficulty comes to mind instead. Let us hear that difficulty calmly. Good advice needs to meet the reality of life, including the limitations we face. Now imagine someone we love asking that question. Would our answer help them act, or simply leave them feeling scolded? Here we learn to convey the truth in a way that can be received. We also need honesty that gives direction when speaking to ourselves, so that understanding a problem gives us courage to begin putting it right.

Dear congregation, try looking at our own journey with both honesty and compassion. In the matter of carrying reminders from the gathering into the journey home, we may have made small progress for which we have never given thanks. There may also be a mistake we keep wanting to hide. Both can teach us without being put on display. Give thanks for the help that has already come, then examine what needs improving. Do not compare our whole journey with a fragment of someone else's life. We have real responsibilities today. Recognizing our part allows reflection to move into action, so regret need not remain a thought circling endlessly without direction.

For closing practice, choose one encounter after returning: family, a neighbour, or someone serving. Determine appropriate attention, perhaps listening fully or pausing before an angry reply. Afterwards, appreciate remaining ability and notice what needs improvement. If difficult, ask help with proper manners. May this learning journey make reminders of Allah easier to find, and may heard advice gain a place in words and actions benefiting others.

Dear congregation, if we want to take one task home from this discussion of carrying reminders from the gathering into the journey home, choose something we can truly do. There is no need to announce it now. We can decide after getting home, when we have a fuller picture of our circumstances. Make the step small enough for us to know when it will be done. If there are obstacles, consider what reasonable help we need. We may also ask a trusted person to remind us respectfully. Change requires our involvement, as well as a heart that feels inspired. Let us accompany a good intention with preparation that makes it easier to carry out.

Dear friends, we can pause before answering a question that feels close to home. Sometimes our first answer comes from a habit of defending ourselves. Given time, we can hear the advice more clearly. We do not have to make everyone speak immediately. Some people think more easily in silence, while others are helped by asking questions. What matters is making room to understand, then choosing a step sincerely. We want to learn in a way that preserves good manners and makes our responsibilities clearer.
REINFORCING THE MESSAGE AND CLOSING SUPPLICATION

Dear friends, our problems may not be resolved immediately after this lesson. Yet may we gain a clearer way of seeing the matter of carrying reminders from the gathering into the journey home. That clarity can help us take the next step more responsibly. Carry a sound understanding, then make room for the process of learning. If help is needed, seek it properly. If we can already begin, act without waiting for every circumstance to become perfect. We have an opportunity to make an effort today, and we continue asking Allah for help. With that hope, let us bring this meeting to a close with supplication and a willingness to put the lesson into practice.

Let us go home with one earnest step. May Allah accept learning time, protect intentions, and help bring benefit to family and neighbours. May encountered creation recall its Creator.
